pob.text: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz[a], which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

spob.text: This is the vision Isaiah son of Amoz saw about Judah and Jerusalem.[a] He saw it during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the vision concerning Judah and Jerusalem that Isaiah son of Amoz saw during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

pob.text: Hear[a], O heavens, and give ear, O earth, for Yahweh has spoken: “I have reared children and brought them up[b], but they have rebelled against me.”

spob.text:
Listen, heavens! Pay attention, earth, because Yahweh has spoken:

“I raised children and made them great,[a]
but they rebelled against me.”

public_domain_references.web: Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh has spoken: “I have nourished and brought up children and they have rebelled against me.
public_domain_references.asv: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth; for Jehovah hath spoken: I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.

public_domain_references.brenton: Hear, O heaven, and hearken, O earth: for the Lord has spoken, [saying], I have begotten and reared up children, but they have rebelled against me.

pob.text: An ox knows its owner[a], and a donkey its master's feeding trough; Israel does not know[b]; my people do not understand.

spob.text: An ox knows its owner. A donkey knows its master's feeding trough. But Israel does not know. My people do not understand.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master’s manger, but Israel does not know; My people do not understand.”
public_domain_references.web: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know. My people don’t consider.”
public_domain_references.asv: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib; [but] Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.
public_domain_references.kjv: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master’s crib: [but] Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.
public_domain_references.brenton: The ox knows his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel does not know me, and the people has not regarded me.

pob.text: Ah[a], sinful nation, a people heavy with iniquity, offspring of evildoers[b], children who act corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh; they have despised the Holy One of Israel[e][d][c]; they have turned backward.

spob.text: Ah,[a] what a sinful nation! They are a people weighed down by sin, descendants of evildoers, children whose actions are corrupt. They have abandoned Yahweh[b] and despised the Holy One of Israel. They have turned their backs on him.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: Alas, O sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a brood of evildoers, children of depravity! They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on Him.
public_domain_references.web: Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh. They have despised the Holy One of Israel. They are estranged and backward.
public_domain_references.asv: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evil-doers, children that deal corruptly! they have forsaken Jehovah, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are estranged [and gone] backward.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters: they have forsaken the LORD, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.
public_domain_references.brenton: Ah sinful nation, a people full of sins, an evil seed, lawless children: ye have forsaken the Lord, and provoked the Holy One of Israel.

pob.text: Why should you be struck again? You continue in rebellion. The whole head is sick[a], and the whole heart is faint.

spob.text: Why should you suffer more blows? You keep rebelling. Your whole head is sick,[a] and your whole heart is faint.

public_domain_references.bsb: Why do you want more beatings? Why do you keep rebelling? Your head has a massive wound, and your whole heart is afflicted.
public_domain_references.web: Why should you be beaten more, that you revolt more and more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
public_domain_references.asv: Why will ye be still stricken, that ye revolt more and more? the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.
public_domain_references.brenton: Why should ye be smitten [any] more, transgressing more and more? the whole head is pained, and the whole heart sad.

pob.text: From the sole of the foot even to the head[a], there is no soundness in it—only wounds and bruises and fresh blows; they have not been pressed out, or bandaged[d][c][b], or softened with oil.

spob.text: From the sole of the foot to the head, not one part of the body is healthy.[a] It is covered with wounds, bruises, and fresh injuries from blows.[b] These injuries have not been pressed to drain them, bandaged, or softened with oil.

public_domain_references.bsb: From the sole of your foot to the top of your head, there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and festering sores neither cleansed nor bandaged nor soothed with oil.
public_domain_references.web: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it, but wounds, welts, and open sores. They haven’t been closed, bandaged, or soothed with oil.
public_domain_references.asv: From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; [but] wounds, and bruises, and fresh stripes: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with oil.
public_domain_references.kjv: From the sole of the foot even unto the head [there is] no soundness in it; [but] wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.
public_domain_references.brenton: From the feet to the head, there is no soundness in them; neither wound, nor bruise, nor festering ulcer [are healed]: it is not possible to apply a plaister, nor oil, nor bandages.

pob.text: Your land is a desolation[a]; your cities are burned with fire. Your soil—before your very eyes—strangers are devouring it, and it is a desolation[b], like an overthrow by strangers.

spob.text: Your land is devastated. Your cities have been burned with fire. Before your very eyes, foreigners are devouring what your soil produces. The land is devastated, like an overthrow by foreigners.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Your land is desolate; your cities are burned with fire. Foreigners devour your fields before you— a desolation demolished by strangers.
public_domain_references.web: Your country is desolate. Your cities are burned with fire. Strangers devour your land in your presence and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
public_domain_references.asv: Your country is desolate; your cities are burned with fire; your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
public_domain_references.kjv: Your country [is] desolate, your cities [are] burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and [it is] desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
public_domain_references.brenton: Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is made desolate, overthrown by strange nations.

pob.text: And daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard[a], like a hut in a cucumber field[c][b], like a besieged city.

spob.text: Daughter Zion[a] has been left alone, like a temporary shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field[b], and like a city under siege.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: And the Daughter of Zion is abandoned like a shelter in a vineyard, like a shack in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.
public_domain_references.web: The daughter of Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged city.
public_domain_references.asv: And the daughter of Zion is left as a booth in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.
public_domain_references.brenton: The daughter of Sion shall be deserted as a tent in a vineyard, and as a storehouse of fruits in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city.

pob.text: If Yahweh of hosts had not left us a very small remnant[a], we would have become like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.

spob.text: Yahweh of Hosts[a] left only a very small remnant[b] of us. If he had not, we would have become like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.

public_domain_references.bsb: Unless the LORD of Hosts had left us a few survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah.
public_domain_references.web: Unless Yahweh of Armies had left to us a very small remnant, we would have been as Sodom. We would have been like Gomorrah.
public_domain_references.asv: Except Jehovah of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
public_domain_references.kjv: Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, [and] we should have been like unto Gomorrah.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if the Lord of Sabaoth had not left us a seed, we should have been as Sodoma, and we should have been made like to Gomorrha.

pob.text: Hear the word of Yahweh[a], rulers of Sodom; give ear to the instruction of our God[b], people of Gomorrah.

spob.text: Listen to the word of Yahweh, you rulers of Sodom.[a] Pay attention to the instruction of our God,[b] you people of Gomorrah.

public_domain_references.bsb: Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom; listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
public_domain_references.web: Hear Yahweh’s word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!
public_domain_references.asv: Hear the word of Jehovah, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Hear the word of the LORD, ye rulers of Sodom; give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah.
public_domain_references.brenton: Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodoma; attend to the law of God, thou people of Gomorrha.

pob.text: Why are your many sacrifices to me? says Yahweh[a]. I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals[b]; and in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats I do not delight.

spob.text: “What use are your many sacrifices to me?” says Yahweh. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of well-fed animals. I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, lambs, and goats.”

pob.text: When you come to appear before me[a], who has required this from your hand: trampling my courts?

pob.text: Do not continue bringing worthless grain offerings[a]; incense is an abomination to me. New moon and Sabbath[b], the calling of an assembly—I cannot endure iniquity and solemn assembly.

spob.text: Do not bring any more worthless offerings of grain. Incense is detestable to me. You observe new moon festivals and Sabbaths and call people together for worship. But I cannot endure evil and a solemn worship gathering.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Bring your worthless offerings no more; your incense is detestable to Me— your New Moons, Sabbaths, and convocations. I cannot endure iniquity in a solemn assembly.

pob.text: Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hates[a]; they have become a burden to me; I am weary of bearing them.

spob.text: I hate your new moon celebrations and appointed festivals with my whole being. They have become a heavy load to me; I am tired of carrying them.

pob.text: And when you spread out your palms[a], I hide my eyes from you; even though you multiply prayers, I am not listening[c][b]. Your hands are full of blood.

pob.text: Learn to do good; seek justice[a], correct the oppressor; judge for the fatherless, plead for the widow.

pob.text: Come now[a], and let us reason together, says Yahweh: though your sins are like scarlet, they will become white like snow; though they are red like crimson[b], they will become like wool.

public_domain_references.web: “Come now, and let’s reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.

public_domain_references.brenton: And come, let us reason together, saith the Lord: and though your sins be as purple, I will make them white as snow; and though they be as scarlet, I will make [them] white as wool.

public_domain_references.web: Woe to those who are mighty to drink wine, and champions at mixing strong drink;
public_domain_references.asv: Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink;
public_domain_references.kjv: Woe unto [them that are] mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:
public_domain_references.brenton: Woe to the strong [ones] of you that drink wine, and the mighty [ones] that mingle strong drink:

pob.text: who acquit the wicked for a bribe[a], and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him.

spob.text: who acquit the wicked for a bribe and take away from a righteous person the righteousness that belongs to him.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deprive the innocent of justice.
public_domain_references.web: who acquit the guilty for a bribe, but deny justice for the innocent!
public_domain_references.asv: that justify the wicked for a bribe, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!
public_domain_references.kjv: Which justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!
public_domain_references.brenton: who justify the ungodly for rewards, and take away the righteousness of the righteous.

pob.text: Therefore[a], as the tongue of fire devours stubble, and dry grass sinks before the flame, so their root will become rot, and their blossom will go up like dust; for they have rejected the law of Yahweh of hosts[b], and have despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

spob.text: Therefore, just as a tongue of fire devours stubble and dry grass collapses before the flame, their root will rot,[a] and their blossom will rise like dust. This will happen because they rejected the law of Yahweh of heaven’s armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore, as a tongue of fire consumes the straw, and as dry grass shrivels in the flame, so their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust; for they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore as the tongue of fire devours the stubble, and as the dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust, because they have rejected the law of Yahweh of Armies, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore as the tongue of fire devoureth the stubble, and as the dry grass sinketh down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust; because they have rejected the law of Jehovah of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore as the fire devoureth the stubble, and the flame consumeth the chaff, [so] their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall go up as dust: because they have cast away the law of the LORD of hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore as stubble shall be burnt by a coal of fire, and shall be consumed by a violent flame, their root shall be as chaff, and their flower shall go up as dust: for they rejected the law of the Lord of hosts, and insulted the word of the Holy One of Israel.

pob.text: Therefore the anger of Yahweh burned against his people[a], and he stretched out his hand against them and struck them; the mountains quaked, and their corpses were like refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this, his anger has not turned away, and his hand is still stretched out.

spob.text: So Yahweh’s anger burned against his people. He reached out his hand against them and struck them. The mountains shook, and their dead bodies were like refuse[a] in the streets. Even after all this, his anger has not turned away. His hand is still stretched out against them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people; His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lay like refuse in the streets. Despite all this, His anger is not turned away; His hand is still upraised.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore Yahweh’s anger burns against his people, and he has stretched out his hand against them and has struck them. The mountains tremble, and their dead bodies are as refuse in the middle of the streets. For all this, his anger is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore is the anger of Jehovah kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them; and the mountains tremble, and their dead bodies are as refuse in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore is the anger of the LORD kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them: and the hills did tremble, and their carcases [were] torn in the midst of the streets. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand [is] stretched out still.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore the Lord of hosts was greatly angered against his people, and he reached forth his hand upon them, and smote them: and the mountains were troubled, and their carcases were as dung in the midst of the way: yet for all this his anger has not been turned away, but his hand is yet raised.

pob.text: He will raise a signal for the nations from far away[a], and whistle for them from the end of the earth; and behold, quickly, swiftly[c][b], it comes.

spob.text: He will raise a signal to summon nations from far away. He will whistle to call them from the farthest reaches of the earth. Look! The invading force[a] comes quickly and swiftly.

public_domain_references.bsb: He lifts a banner for the distant nations and whistles for those at the ends of the earth. Behold—how speedily and swiftly they come!
public_domain_references.web: He will lift up a banner to the nations from far away, and he will whistle for them from the end of the earth. Behold, they will come speedily and swiftly.
public_domain_references.asv: And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss for them from the end of the earth; and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly:
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore shall he lift up a signal to the nations that are afar, and shall hiss for them from the end of the earth; and, behold, they are coming very quickly.

pob.text: None among them is weary[a], and none stumbles; none slumbers or sleeps; the belt at his waist is not loosened[b], and the strap of his sandals is not broken.

spob.text: No one in the army grows tired or stumbles. No one dozes or sleeps. No soldier’s belt comes loose, and no sandal strap breaks.

public_domain_references.bsb: None of them grows weary or stumbles; no one slumbers or sleeps. No belt is loose and no sandal strap is broken.
public_domain_references.web: No one shall be weary nor stumble among them; no one shall slumber nor sleep, neither shall the belt of their waist be untied, nor the strap of their sandals be broken,
public_domain_references.asv: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:
public_domain_references.kjv: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:
public_domain_references.brenton: They shall not hunger nor be weary, neither shall they slumber nor sleep; neither shall they loose their girdles from their loins, neither shall their shoe-latchets be broken.

pob.text: whose arrows are sharpened[a], and all his bows are bent; the hooves of his horses are considered like flint[c][b], and his wheels like the whirlwind.

spob.text: His arrows are sharp, and all his bows are ready to shoot. His horses’ hooves are as hard as flint, and his chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.

public_domain_references.bsb: Their arrows are sharpened, and all their bows are strung. The hooves of their horses are like flint; their chariot wheels are like a whirlwind.
public_domain_references.web: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent. Their horses’ hoofs will be like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind.
public_domain_references.asv: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent; their horses’ hoofs shall be accounted as flint, and their wheels as a whirlwind:
public_domain_references.kjv: Whose arrows [are] sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses’ hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind:
public_domain_references.brenton: Whose arrows are sharp, and their bows bent; their horses' hoofs are counted as solid rock: their chariot-wheels are as a storm.

pob.text: Its roaring is like a lion[a], and it roars like young lions; it growls and seizes prey, and carries it off[b], with none to rescue.

spob.text: It roars like a lion;[a] it roars like young lions. It growls, grabs its prey, and carries it away.[b] No one can rescue the prey.

public_domain_references.bsb: Their roaring is like that of a lion; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey; they carry it away from deliverance.
public_domain_references.web: Their roaring will be like a lioness. They will roar like young lions. Yes, they shall roar, and seize their prey and carry it off, and there will be no one to deliver.
public_domain_references.asv: their roaring shall be like a lioness, they shall roar like young lions; yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and carry it away safe, and there shall be none to deliver.
public_domain_references.kjv: Their roaring [shall be] like a lion, they shall roar like young lions: yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and shall carry [it] away safe, and none shall deliver [it].
public_domain_references.brenton: They rage as lions, and draw nigh as a lion's whelps: and he shall seize, and roar as a wild beast, and he shall cast [them] forth, and there shall be none to deliver them.

pob.text: And he will roar over it on that day like the roaring of the sea[a]; and if one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress[d][c][b], and the light is darkened in its clouds.

spob.text: On that day he will roar over it like the roar of the sea.[a] If anyone looks toward the land, look—there is darkness and distress, and even the light is darkened in its clouds.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: In that day they will roar over it, like the roaring of the sea. If one looks over the land, he will see darkness and distress; even the light will be obscured by clouds.
public_domain_references.web: They will roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea. If one looks to the land, behold, darkness and distress. The light is darkened in its clouds.
public_domain_references.asv: And they shall roar against them in that day like the roaring of the sea: and if one look unto the land, behold, darkness [and] distress; and the light is darkened in the clouds thereof.
public_domain_references.kjv: And in that day they shall roar against them like the roaring of the sea: and if [one] look unto the land, behold darkness [and] sorrow, and the light is darkened in the heavens thereof.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he shall roar on account of them in that day, as the sound of the swelling sea; and they shall look to the land, and, behold, [there shall be] thick darkness in their perplexity.

pob.text: In the year of King Uzziah’s death[a], I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and lifted up[b], and the hem of his robe filled the temple.

spob.text: In the year King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord, high and lifted up, sitting on a throne. The hem of his robe filled the temple.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord seated on a throne, high and exalted; and the train of His robe filled the temple.
public_domain_references.web: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
public_domain_references.asv: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
public_domain_references.kjv: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the year in which king Ozias died, [that] I saw the Lord sitting on a high and exalted throne, and the house was full of his glory.

pob.text: Seraphim were standing above him. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face[a], and with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.

spob.text: The seraphim[a] were standing above him. Each one had six wings. He used two to cover his face, two more to cover his feet, and the remaining two to fly.

public_domain_references.bsb: Above Him stood seraphim, each having six wings: With two wings they covered their faces, with two they covered their feet, and with two they were flying.
public_domain_references.web: Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.
public_domain_references.asv: Above him stood the seraphim: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.
public_domain_references.kjv: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.
public_domain_references.brenton: And seraphs stood round about him: each one had six wings: and with two they covered [their] face, and with two they covered [their] feet, and with two they flew.

pob.text: And one called to another and said: “Holy[a], holy, holy is Yahweh of hosts[b]; the whole earth is full of his glory.”

spob.text:
One called out to another:

“Holy, holy, holy is Yahweh,[a] who commands all the forces of heaven and earth.[b] The whole earth is full of his glory.”

public_domain_references.bsb: And they were calling out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; all the earth is full of His glory.”
public_domain_references.web: One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
public_domain_references.asv: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is Jehovah of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
public_domain_references.kjv: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, [is] the LORD of hosts: the whole earth [is] full of his glory.
public_domain_references.brenton: And one cried to the other, and they said, Holy, holy, holy, [is the] Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.

pob.text: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the sound of the one calling[b][a], and the house was filled with smoke.

spob.text: At the sound of the one calling out, the foundations at the doorways shook, and the house was filled with smoke.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: At the sound of their voices the doorposts and thresholds shook, and the temple was filled with smoke.
public_domain_references.web: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke.
public_domain_references.asv: And the foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the lintel shook at the voice they uttered, and the house was filled with smoke.

pob.text: And I said[a], “Woe is me, for I am ruined; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King[b], Yahweh of Armies.”

spob.text: Then I said, “Woe is me! I am ruined,[a] because I am a man with unclean lips, and I live among a people with unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies![b]”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I said: “Woe is me, for I am ruined, because I am a man of unclean lips dwelling among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Hosts.”
public_domain_references.web: Then I said, “Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips and I live among a people of unclean lips, for my eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies!”
public_domain_references.asv: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, Jehovah of hosts.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then said I, Woe [is] me! for I am undone; because I [am] a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I said, Woe is me, for I am pricked to the heart; for being a man, and having unclean lips, I dwell in the midst of a people having unclean lips; and I have seen with mine eyes the King, the Lord of hosts.

pob.text: Then one of the seraphim flew to me[a], and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken from the altar with tongs.

spob.text: Then one of the seraphim flew to me. He held a glowing coal[a] in his hand. He had taken it from the altar with tongs.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, and in his hand was a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
public_domain_references.web: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.
public_domain_references.asv: Then flew one of the seraphim unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:
public_domain_references.kjv: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, [which] he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:
public_domain_references.brenton: And there was sent to me one of the seraphs, and he had in his hand a coal, which he had taken off the altar with the tongs:

pob.text: And he touched my mouth and said, “Look, this has touched your lips; your guilt is removed, and your sin is atoned for.”

spob.text: Then he touched my mouth with it and said, “Look! It has touched your lips. Your guilt is gone, and your sin has been atoned for.”

public_domain_references.bsb: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”
public_domain_references.web: He touched my mouth with it, and said, “Behold, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven.”
public_domain_references.asv: and he touched my mouth with it, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin forgiven.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he laid [it] upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.
public_domain_references.brenton: and he touched my mouth, and said, Behold, this has touched thy lips, and will take away thine iniquities, and will purge off thy sins.

pob.text: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying[a], “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I[b]. Send me.”

spob.text: Then I heard the Lord’s voice. He said, “Who should I send? Who will go for us?”[a] I answered, “Here I am, ready to go. Send me.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”
public_domain_references.web: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”
public_domain_references.asv: And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I; send me.
public_domain_references.kjv: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here [am] I; send me.
public_domain_references.brenton: And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go to this people? And I said, Behold, I am [here], send me. And he said, Go, and say to this people,

pob.text: And he said[a], “Go, and say to this people: ‘Keep hearing, but do not understand; keep seeing, but do not perceive.’”

spob.text: And he said,[a] “Go and tell this people: ‘Keep hearing, but do not understand. Keep seeing, but do not perceive.’”

public_domain_references.bsb: And He replied: “Go and tell this people, ‘Be ever hearing, but never understanding; be ever seeing, but never perceiving.’
public_domain_references.web: He said, “Go, and tell this people, ‘You hear indeed, but don’t understand. You see indeed, but don’t perceive.’
public_domain_references.asv: And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not.
public_domain_references.brenton: Ye shall hear indeed, but ye shall not understand; and ye shall see indeed, but ye shall not perceive.

pob.text: Make the heart of this people dull[a], and make their ears heavy, and blind their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back[c][b], and be healed.

spob.text: Make the heart of this people dull and unresponsive. Make their ears heavy and their eyes blind,[a] so that they do not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, or understand with their heart, turn back,[b] and be healed.

public_domain_references.bsb: Make the hearts of this people calloused; deafen their ears and close their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn and be healed.”
public_domain_references.web: Make the heart of this people fat. Make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.”
public_domain_references.asv: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn again, and be healed.
public_domain_references.kjv: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the heart of this people has become gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes have they closed; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.

pob.text: Then I said[a], “Until when, Lord?” And he said, “Until cities lie waste, without inhabitant, and houses without man, and the land is laid waste[b], a desolation.”

spob.text: Then I said, “Lord, until when?”[a] He answered, “Until the cities lie in ruins, with no one living in them; the houses have no one in them; and the land is devastated and desolate.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Then I asked: “How long, O Lord?” And He replied: “Until the cities lie ruined and without inhabitant, until the houses are left unoccupied and the land is desolate and ravaged,
public_domain_references.web: Then I said, “Lord, how long?” He answered, “Until cities are waste without inhabitant, houses without man, the land becomes utterly waste,
public_domain_references.asv: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until cities be waste without inhabitant, and houses without man, and the land become utterly waste,
public_domain_references.kjv: Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate,
public_domain_references.brenton: And I said, How long, O Lord? And he said, Until the cities be deserted by reason of their not being inhabited, and the houses by reason of there being no men, and the land shall be left desolate.

pob.text: And Yahweh will remove people far away[b][a], and the forsaken places will be many in the midst of the land.

spob.text: Yahweh will send the people far away, and many places throughout the land will be left deserted.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: until the LORD has driven men far away and the land is utterly forsaken.
public_domain_references.web: and Yahweh has removed men far away, and the forsaken places are many within the land.
public_domain_references.asv: and Jehovah have removed men far away, and the forsaken places be many in the midst of the land.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the LORD have removed men far away, and [there be] a great forsaking in the midst of the land.
public_domain_references.brenton: And after this God shall remove the men far off, and they that are left upon the land shall be multiplied.

pob.text: And though a tenth remains in it[a], it will again be for burning, like a terebinth or like an oak whose stump remains when it is felled. The holy seed is its stump.

spob.text: Even if a tenth remains in the land, that tenth will again be burned away. It will be like a terebinth or an oak whose stump remains when it is cut down.[a] The holy seed is that stump.

public_domain_references.bsb: And though a tenth remains in the land, it will be burned again. As the terebinth and oak leave stumps when felled, so the holy seed will be a stump in the land.”
public_domain_references.web: If there is a tenth left in it, that also will in turn be consumed, as a terebinth, and as an oak whose stump remains when they are cut down, so the holy seed is its stump.”
public_domain_references.asv: And if there be yet a tenth in it, it also shall in turn be eaten up: as a terebinth, and as an oak, whose stock remaineth, when they are felled; so the holy seed is the stock thereof.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ But yet in it [shall be] a tenth, and [it] shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance [is] in them, when they cast [their leaves: so] the holy seed [shall be] the substance thereof.
public_domain_references.brenton: And yet there shall be a tenth upon it, and again it shall be for a spoil, as a turpentine tree, and as an acorn when it falls out of its husk.

pob.text: And it happened in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham[a], son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to wage war against it[b], but they were not able to fight against it.

spob.text: During the reign of Ahaz, the son of Jotham and grandson of Uzziah, king of Judah, King Rezin of Aram[a] and King Pekah of Israel, the son of Remaliah, marched to Jerusalem to make war against it. But he[b] was not able to fight against it.

public_domain_references.bsb: Now in the days that Ahaz son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, was king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram marched up to wage war against Jerusalem. He was accompanied by Pekah son of Remaliah the king of Israel, but he could not overpower the city.
public_domain_references.web: In the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
public_domain_references.asv: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up to Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
public_domain_references.kjv: And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, [that] Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the days of Achaz [the son] of Joatham, the son of Ozias, king of Juda, there came up Rasin king of Aram, and Phakee son of Romelias, king of Israel, against Jerusalem to war against it, but they could not take it.

public_domain_references.brenton: For behold! the day of the Lord is coming which cannot be escaped, [a day] of wrath and anger, to make the world desolate, and to destroy sinners out of it.

pob.text: For the stars of the heavens and their constellations will not give their light; the sun is darkened at its rising[a], and the moon will not make its light shine.

spob.text: For the stars in the sky and their constellations[a] will give no light. The sun is darkened as it rises, and the moon will not make its light shine.

public_domain_references.bsb: For the stars of heaven and their constellations will not give their light. The rising sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light.
public_domain_references.web: For the stars of the sky and its constellations will not give their light. The sun will be darkened in its going out, and the moon will not cause its light to shine.
public_domain_references.asv: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light; the sun shall be darkened in its going forth, and the moon shall not cause its light to shine.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the stars of heaven, and Orion, and all the host of heaven, shall not give their light; and it shall be dark at sunrise, and the moon shall not give her light.

public_domain_references.brenton: And I will command evils for the whole world, and [will visit] their sins on the ungodly: and I will destroy the pride of transgressors, and will bring low the pride of the haughty.

public_domain_references.asv: I will make a man more rare than fine gold, even a man than the pure gold of Ophir.
public_domain_references.kjv: I will make a man more precious than fine gold; even a man than the golden wedge of Ophir.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they that are left shall be more precious than gold tried in the fire; and a man shall be more precious than the stone that is in Suphir.

pob.text: Therefore I will make the heavens tremble[a], and the earth will shake from its place, at the fury of Yahweh of Armies, in the day of his burning anger.

public_domain_references.brenton: For the heaven shall be enraged, and the earth shall be shaken from her foundation, because of the fierce anger of the Lord of hosts, in the day in which his wrath shall come on.

pob.text: And it will be like a hunted gazelle[a], and like sheep with no one to gather them; each man will turn to his own people[b], and each will flee to his own land.

public_domain_references.brenton: For whosoever shall be taken shall be overcome; and they that are gathered together shall fall by the sword.

public_domain_references.web: In their streets, they clothe themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping abundantly.
public_domain_references.asv: In their streets they gird themselves with sackcloth; on their housetops, and in their broad places, every one waileth, weeping abundantly.
public_domain_references.kjv: In their streets they shall gird themselves with sackcloth: on the tops of their houses, and in their streets, every one shall howl, weeping abundantly.
public_domain_references.brenton: Gird yourselves with sackcloth in her streets: and lament upon her roofs, and in her streets, and in her ways; howl all of you with weeping.

pob.text: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out[a]; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out[b]; his soul trembles within him.

spob.text: Cries of distress rise from Heshbon and Elealeh and are heard as far as Jahaz. So Moab’s armed men cry out; Moab trembles deep within.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voices are heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the soldiers of Moab cry out; their souls tremble within.
public_domain_references.web: Heshbon cries out with Elealeh. Their voice is heard even to Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud. Their souls tremble within them.
public_domain_references.asv: And Heshbon crieth out, and Elealeh; their voice is heard even unto Jahaz: therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud; his soul trembleth within him.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Heshbon shall cry, and Elealeh: their voice shall be heard [even] unto Jahaz: therefore the armed soldiers of Moab shall cry out; his life shall be grievous unto him.
public_domain_references.brenton: For Esebon and Eleale have cried: their voice was heard to Jassa: therefore the loins of the region of Moab cry aloud; her soul shall know.

pob.text: My heart cries out for Moab[a]; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. For they go up the ascent of Luhith with weeping[c][b]; for on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction.

spob.text: My heart cries out for Moab. Her refugees[a] flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah.[b] They climb the ascent of Luhith, weeping. On the road to Horonaim, they raise a cry of ruin.

public_domain_references.bsb: My heart cries out over Moab; her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. With weeping they ascend the slope of Luhith; they lament their destruction on the road to Horonaim.
public_domain_references.web: My heart cries out for Moab! Her nobles flee to Zoar, to Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Luhith with weeping; for on the way to Horonaim, they raise up a cry of destruction.
public_domain_references.asv: My heart crieth out for Moab; her nobles [flee] unto Zoar, to Eglath-shelishi-yah: for by the ascent of Luhith with weeping they go up; for in the way of Horonaim they raise up a cry of destruction.
public_domain_references.kjv: My heart shall cry out for Moab; his fugitives [shall flee] unto Zoar, an heifer of three years old: for by the mounting up of Luhith with weeping shall they go it up; for in the way of Horonaim they shall raise up a cry of destruction.
public_domain_references.brenton: The heart of the region of Moab cries within her to Segor; for it is [as] a heifer of three years old: and on the ascent of Luith they shall go up to thee weeping by the way of Aroniim: she cries, Destruction, and trembling.

pob.text: For the waters of Nimrim will become desolations[a], for the grass is dried up, the vegetation is gone, and no green thing remains.

spob.text: For the waters of Nimrim will become desolate.[a] The grass has dried up, the fresh growth is gone, and nothing green remains.

public_domain_references.bsb: The waters of Nimrim are dried up, and the grass is withered; the vegetation is gone, and the greenery is no more.
public_domain_references.web: For the waters of Nimrim will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass fails, there is no green thing.
public_domain_references.asv: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate; for the grass is withered away, the tender grass faileth, there is no green thing.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the waters of Nimrim shall be desolate: for the hay is withered away, the grass faileth, there is no green thing.
public_domain_references.brenton: The water of Nemerim shall be desolate, and the grass thereof shall fail: for there shall be no green grass.

pob.text: Therefore the abundance they have gained and what they have stored up they carry away over the Brook of the Willows[a][b].

spob.text: So they carry away the abundance they have gained, along with what they have stored up, across the Brook of the Willows.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: So they carry their wealth and belongings over the Brook of the Willows.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the brook of the willows.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall they carry away over the brook of the willows.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have laid up, shall they carry away to the brook of the willows.
public_domain_references.brenton: Shall [Moab] even thus be delivered? for I [will] bring the Arabians upon the valley, and they shall take it.

pob.text: For the outcry has gone around the border of Moab[a]; its wailing reaches as far as Eglaim[b], and its wailing to Beer-elim.

spob.text: For the cry of distress has spread all around Moab’s border. The wailing reaches as far as Eglaim and Beer-elim.

public_domain_references.bsb: For their outcry echoes to the border of Moab. Their wailing reaches Eglaim; it is heard in Beer-elim.
public_domain_references.web: For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab, its wailing to Eglaim, and its wailing to Beer Elim.
public_domain_references.asv: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the wailing thereof unto Eglaim, and the wailing thereof unto Beer-elim.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the cry is gone round about the borders of Moab; the howling thereof unto Eglaim, and the howling thereof unto Beer-elim.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the cry has reached the border of the region of Moab, [even] of Agalim; and her howling [has gone] as far as the well of Ælim.

pob.text: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood[a], for I will bring more upon Dimon: a lion upon the fugitives of Moab[c][b], and upon the remnant of the land.

spob.text: For Dimon’s waters are full of blood.[a] Indeed, I will bring still more upon Dimon:[b] a lion will come against those fleeing from Moab and those who remain in the land.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: The waters of Dimon are full of blood, but I will bring more upon Dimon— a lion upon the fugitives of Moab and upon the remnant of the land.
public_domain_references.web: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more on Dimon, a lion on those of Moab who escape, and on the remnant of the land.
public_domain_references.asv: For the waters of Dimon are full of blood; for I will bring yet more upon Dimon, a lion upon them of Moab that escape, and upon the remnant of the land.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the waters of Dimon shall be full of blood: for I will bring more upon Dimon, lions upon him that escapeth of Moab, and upon the remnant of the land.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the water of Dimon shall be filled with blood: for I will bring Arabians upon Dimon, and I will take away the seed of Moab, and Ariel, and the remnant of Adama.

pob.text: Send a lamb to the ruler of the land[b][a], from Sela in the wilderness to the mountain of daughter Zion.

spob.text: Send a lamb[b] from Sela[a] through the wilderness to the ruler of the land—to the mountain of Daughter Zion.

public_domain_references.bsb: Send the tribute lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela in the desert to the mount of Daughter Zion.
public_domain_references.web: Send the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, to the mountain of the daughter of Zion.
public_domain_references.asv: Send ye the lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.
public_domain_references.kjv: Send ye the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion.
public_domain_references.brenton: I will send as it were reptiles on the land: is [not] the mount of the daughter of Sion a desolate rock?

pob.text: And like a wandering bird[a], like a scattered nest[b], so the daughters of Moab will be at the fords of the Arnon.

spob.text: At the crossings of the Arnon River, the daughters of Moab will be like a wandering bird, like a nest scattered and abandoned.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Like fluttering birds pushed out of the nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon:
public_domain_references.web: For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
public_domain_references.asv: For it shall be that, as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so shall the daughters of Moab be at the fords of the Arnon.
public_domain_references.kjv: For it shall be, [that], as a wandering bird cast out of the nest, [so] the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon.
public_domain_references.brenton: For thou shalt be as a young bird taken away from a bird that has flown: [even] thou shalt be [so], daughter of Moab: and then do thou, O Arnon,

pob.text: Bring counsel[a]; make a decision. Make your shadow like the night in the middle of noon; hide the outcasts[c][b]; do not betray the fugitive.

spob.text: Give counsel and make a decision.[a] Make your shadow like night even at high noon. Hide the outcasts, and do not betray the fugitive.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: “Give us counsel; render a decision. Shelter us at noonday with shade as dark as night. Hide the refugees; do not betray the one who flees.
public_domain_references.web: Give counsel! Execute justice! Make your shade like the night in the middle of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don’t betray the fugitive!
public_domain_references.asv: Give counsel, execute justice; make thy shade as the night in the midst of the noonday; hide the outcasts; betray not the fugitive.
public_domain_references.kjv: Take counsel, execute judgment; make thy shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday; hide the outcasts; bewray not him that wandereth.
public_domain_references.brenton: take farther counsel, and continually make thou a shelter from grief: they flee in darkness at mid-day; they are amazed; be not thou led captive.

pob.text: Let the outcasts of Moab stay with you; be a shelter for them from the destroyer. For the oppressor has come to an end[a], destruction has ceased, those who trample have vanished from the land.

spob.text: Let the people driven out of Moab stay with you. Give them shelter from the destroyer. The oppressor has come to an end, destruction has stopped, and those who trample have disappeared from the land.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Let my fugitives stay with you; be a refuge for Moab from the destroyer.” When the oppressor has gone, destruction has ceased, and the oppressors have vanished from the land,
public_domain_references.web: Let my outcasts dwell with you! As for Moab, be a hiding place for him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortionist is brought to nothing. Destruction ceases. The oppressors are consumed out of the land.
public_domain_references.asv: Let mine outcasts dwell with thee; as for Moab, be thou a covert to him from the face of the destroyer. For the extortioner is brought to nought, destruction ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land.
public_domain_references.kjv: Let mine outcasts dwell with thee, Moab; be thou a covert to them from the face of the spoiler: for the extortioner is at an end, the spoiler ceaseth, the oppressors are consumed out of the land.
public_domain_references.brenton: The fugitives of Moab shall sojourn with thee; they shall be to you a shelter from the face of the pursuer: for thine alliance has been taken away, and the oppressing ruler has perished from off the earth.

pob.text: A throne will be established in steadfast love[a], and one will sit on it in faithfulness in the tent of David[c][b], judging and seeking justice and swift to do righteousness.

spob.text: A throne will be made secure in steadfast love.[a] Someone will sit on it in David’s tent and rule faithfully. He will judge, pursue justice, and be quick to do what is right.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: in loving devotion a throne will be established in the tent of David. A judge seeking justice and hastening righteousness will sit on it in faithfulness.
public_domain_references.web: A throne will be established in loving kindness. One will sit on it in truth, in the tent of David, judging, seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.
public_domain_references.asv: And a throne shall be established in lovingkindness; and one shall sit thereon in truth, in the tent of David, judging, and seeking justice, and swift to do righteousness.
public_domain_references.kjv: And in mercy shall the throne be established: and he shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and seeking judgment, and hasting righteousness.
public_domain_references.brenton: And a throne shall be established with mercy; and one shall sit upon it with truth in the tabernacle of David, judging, and earnestly seeking judgments, and hasting righteousness.

pob.text: We have heard of the pride of Moab—how very proud he is—of his arrogance[a], his pride, and his fury; his boasts are not so.

spob.text: We have heard how proud Moab is—extremely proud. We have heard of his arrogance, pride, and fury. But his boasts do not match reality.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his overflowing arrogance. But his boasting is empty.
public_domain_references.web: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his wrath. His boastings are nothing.
public_domain_references.asv: We have heard of the pride of Moab, [that] he is very proud; even of his arrogancy, and his pride, and his wrath; his boastings are nought.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ We have heard of the pride of Moab; [he is] very proud: [even] of his haughtiness, and his pride, and his wrath: [but] his lies [shall] not [be] so.
public_domain_references.brenton: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud. I have cut off his pride: thy prophecy shall not be thus, [no] not thus.

pob.text: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab; all of it will wail. You will moan[a] for the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth, utterly stricken.

spob.text: So the people of Moab will wail for Moab; the whole nation will wail. People of Moab, you will moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, utterly crushed.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore let Moab wail; let them wail together for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, you who are utterly stricken.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore Moab will wail for Moab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Kir Hareseth, utterly stricken.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore shall Moab wail for Moab, every one shall wail: for the raisin-cakes of Kir-hareseth shall ye mourn, utterly stricken.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir-hareseth shall ye mourn; surely [they are] stricken.
public_domain_references.brenton: Moab shall howl; for all shall howl in the land of Moab: but thou shalt care for them that dwell in Seth, and thou shalt not be ashamed.

pob.text: For the fields of Heshbon languish[a], the vine of Sibmah as well. The lords of the nations have struck down its choice vines; they reached as far as Jazer, they wandered into the wilderness[c][b]; its shoots spread out and crossed the sea.

spob.text: The fields of Heshbon are wasting away, and so is the vine of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have struck down its best vines.[a] The vines reached as far as Jazer and wandered into the wilderness. Their shoots spread out[b] and crossed the sea.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: For the fields of Heshbon have withered, along with the grapevines of Sibmah. The rulers of the nations have trampled its choicest vines, which had reached as far as Jazer and spread toward the desert. Their shoots had spread out and passed over the sea.
public_domain_references.web: For the fields of Heshbon languish with the vine of Sibmah. The lords of the nations have broken down its choice branches, which reached even to Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness. Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the sea.
public_domain_references.asv: For the fields of Heshbon languish, [and] the vine of Sibmah; the lords of the nations have broken down the choice branches thereof, which reached even unto Jazer, which wandered into the wilderness; its shoots were spread abroad, they passed over the sea.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the fields of Heshbon languish, [and] the vine of Sibmah: the lords of the heathen have broken down the principal plants thereof, they are come [even] unto Jazer, they wandered [through] the wilderness: her branches are stretched out, they are gone over the sea.
public_domain_references.brenton: The plains of Esebon shall mourn, the vine of Sebama: swallowing up the nations, trample ye her vines, even to Jazer: ye shall not come together; wander ye in the desert: they that were sent are deserted, for they have gone over to the sea.

pob.text: Therefore I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah[a]; I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh[b], because over your summer fruit and over your harvest the battle shout has fallen.

spob.text: So I join Jazer in weeping for the vine of Sibmah. Heshbon and Elealeh, I soak you with my tears, because a shout has fallen over your summer fruit and harvest.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: So I weep with Jazer for the vines of Sibmah; I drench Heshbon and Elealeh with my tears. Triumphant shouts have fallen silent over your summer fruit and your harvest.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah. I will water you with my tears, Heshbon, and Elealeh: for on your summer fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sibmah; I will water thee with my tears, O Heshbon, and Elealeh: for upon thy summer fruits and upon thy harvest the [battle] shout is fallen.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Therefore I will bewail with the weeping of Jazer the vine of Sibmah: I will water thee with my tears, O Heshbon, and Elealeh: for the shouting for thy summer fruits and for thy harvest is fallen.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore will I weep as with the weeping of Jazer for the vine of Sebama; Esebon and Eleale have cast down thy trees; for I will trample on thy harvest and on thy vintages, and all [thy plants] shall fall.

pob.text: Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field[a], and in the vineyards no one sings for joy, no one shouts; no treader treads out wine in the presses[b]; I have put an end to the vintage shout.

spob.text: Joy and gladness have been taken away from the fruitful land.[a] No one sings for joy or shouts in the vineyards. No one stomps grapes in the winepresses. I have silenced the grape-harvest shout.

public_domain_references.bsb: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard; no one sings or shouts in the vineyards. No one tramples the grapes in the winepresses; I have put an end to the cheering.
public_domain_references.web: Gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither joyful noise. Nobody will tread out wine in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.
public_domain_references.asv: And gladness is taken away, and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there shall be no singing, neither joyful noise: no treader shall tread out wine in the presses; I have made the [vintage] shout to cease.
public_domain_references.kjv: And gladness is taken away, and joy out of the plentiful field; and in the vineyards there shall be no singing, neither shall there be shouting: the treaders shall tread out no wine in [their] presses; I have made [their vintage] shouting to cease.
public_domain_references.brenton: And gladness and rejoicing shall be taken away from the vineyards; and they shall not rejoice at all in thy vineyards; and they shall not at all tread wine into the vats; for [the vintage] has ceased.

pob.text: Therefore my inward parts moan like a harp for Moab[b][a], and my inner being for Kir-heres.

spob.text: That is why my insides moan like a harp for Moab; deep within me, I moan for Kir-heres.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Therefore my heart laments for Moab like a harp, my inmost being for Kir-heres.
public_domain_references.web: Therefore my heart sounds like a harp for Moab, and my inward parts for Kir Heres.
public_domain_references.asv: Wherefore my heart soundeth like a harp for Moab, and mine inward parts for Kir-heres.
public_domain_references.kjv: Wherefore my bowels shall sound like an harp for Moab, and mine inward parts for Kir-haresh.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore my belly shall sound as a harp for Moab, and thou hast repaired my inward parts as a wall.

pob.text: And when it is seen that Moab is worn out on the high place[a], and he comes to his sanctuary to pray[c][b], he will not be able.

spob.text: When it becomes clear[a] that Moab is worn out at the high place,[b] he will go to his sanctuary and pray, but he will not prevail.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: When Moab appears on the high place, when he wearies himself and enters his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
public_domain_references.web: It will happen that when Moab presents himself, when he wearies himself on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, that he will not prevail.
public_domain_references.asv: And it shall come to pass, when Moab presenteth himself, when he wearieth himself upon the high place, and shall come to his sanctuary to pray, that he shall not prevail.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And it shall come to pass, when it is seen that Moab is weary on the high place, that he shall come to his sanctuary to pray; but he shall not prevail.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it shall be to thy shame, (for Moab is wearied at the altars,) that he shall go in to the idols thereof to pray, but they shall not be at all able to deliver him.

pob.text: This is the word that Yahweh spoke concerning Moab in time past[a].

spob.text: This is the word Yahweh spoke about Moab in the past.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the message that the LORD spoke earlier concerning Moab.
public_domain_references.web: This is the word that Yahweh spoke concerning Moab in time past.
public_domain_references.asv: This is the word that Jehovah spake concerning Moab in time past.
public_domain_references.kjv: This [is] the word that the LORD hath spoken concerning Moab since that time.
public_domain_references.brenton: This is the word which the Lord spoke against Moab, when he spoke.

pob.text: But now Yahweh has spoken[a], saying, “Within three years, like the years of a hired worker, the glory of Moab will be brought low, with all its great multitude; and the remnant will be few, very small[c][b], not mighty.”

spob.text: But now Yahweh has declared: “Within three years—an exact term, like that of a hired worker—Moab’s glory, along with all its great multitude, will be brought low. The remnant will be very few and not strong.”

public_domain_references.bsb: And now the LORD says, “In three years, as a hired worker counts the years, Moab’s splendor will become an object of contempt, with all her many people. And those who are left will be few and feeble.”
public_domain_references.web: But now Yahweh has spoken, saying, “Within three years, as a worker bound by contract would count them, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant will be very small and feeble.”
public_domain_references.asv: But now Jehovah hath spoken, saying, Within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be brought into contempt, with all his great multitude; and the remnant shall be very small and of no account.
public_domain_references.kjv: But now the LORD hath spoken, saying, Within three years, as the years of an hireling, and the glory of Moab shall be contemned, with all that great multitude; and the remnant [shall be] very small [and] feeble.
public_domain_references.brenton: And now I say, In three years, of the years of an hireling, the glory of Moab shall be dishonoured [with] all his great wealth; and he shall be left few in number, and not honoured.

pob.text: An oracle concerning Damascus: Behold[a], Damascus will be removed from being a city[b], and it will become a heap of ruins.

spob.text: A prophetic message about Damascus: Pay attention! Damascus will cease to be a city and become a heap of ruins.

public_domain_references.bsb: This is the burden against Damascus: “Behold, Damascus is no longer a city; it has become a heap of ruins.
public_domain_references.web: The burden of Damascus. “Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it will be a ruinous heap.
public_domain_references.asv: The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.
public_domain_references.kjv: The burden of Damascus. Behold, Damascus is taken away from [being] a city, and it shall be a ruinous heap.
public_domain_references.brenton: The Word against Damascus. Behold, Damascus shall be taken away from among cities, and shall become a ruin;

pob.text: The cities of Aroer are abandoned[a]; they will be for flocks[b], and they will lie down with no one to make them afraid.

spob.text: The cities of Aroer are deserted. They will become pasture for flocks, and the animals will lie down there with no one to frighten them.

public_domain_references.bsb: The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they will be left to the flocks, which will lie down with no one to fear.
public_domain_references.web: The cities of Aroer are forsaken. They will be for flocks, which shall lie down, and no one shall make them afraid.
public_domain_references.asv: The cities of Aroer are forsaken; they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make them afraid.
public_domain_references.kjv: The cities of Aroer [are] forsaken: they shall be for flocks, which shall lie down, and none shall make [them] afraid.
public_domain_references.brenton: abandoned for ever, to [be] a fold and resting-place for flocks, and there shall be none to go after them.

pob.text: And the fortress will cease from Ephraim[a], and the kingdom from Damascus; and the remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the sons of Israel[b], declares Yahweh of hosts.

spob.text: Ephraim’s fortress will be gone, and Damascus’s kingdom will come to an end. What remains of Aram will be like the glory of the people of Israel.[a] The LORD of hosts declares this.

public_domain_references.bsb: The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the sovereignty from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the splendor of the Israelites,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
public_domain_references.web: The fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria. They will be as the glory of the children of Israel,” says Yahweh of Armies.
public_domain_references.asv: And the fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria; they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith Jehovah of hosts.
public_domain_references.kjv: The fortress also shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus, and the remnant of Syria: they shall be as the glory of the children of Israel, saith the LORD of hosts.
public_domain_references.brenton: And she shall no longer be a strong place for Ephraim to flee to, and there shall no longer be a kingdom in Damascus, or a remnant of Syrians; for thou art no better than the children of Israel, [even] than their glory; thus saith the Lord of hosts.

pob.text: And in that day the glory of Jacob will become thin[b][a], and the fatness of his flesh will waste away.

pob.text: And they will be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush[a], their hope, and because of Egypt[c][b], their boast.

public_domain_references.kjv: And they shall be afraid and ashamed of Ethiopia their expectation, and of Egypt their glory.

public_domain_references.web: The inhabitants of this coast land will say in that day, ‘Behold, this is our expectation, where we fled for help to be delivered from the king of Assyria. And we, how will we escape?’”

pob.text: A harsh vision has been declared to me: the betrayer betrays[a], and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; lay siege, Media[b]. I have put an end to all her groaning.

public_domain_references.bsb: A dire vision is declared to me: “The traitor still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys. Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media! I will put an end to all her groaning.”
public_domain_references.web: A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media’s sighing.

public_domain_references.kjv: A grievous vision is declared unto me; the treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth. Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media; all the sighing thereof have I made to cease.

pob.text: Therefore my loins are filled with anguish[a]; pains have seized me like the pains of a woman giving birth. I am bent over from hearing[b]; I am dismayed from seeing.

spob.text: That is why anguish racks my body.[a] Pain grips me like the labor pains of a woman giving birth. What I hear makes me double over; what I see fills me with dismay.

public_domain_references.web: Therefore my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have seized me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am in so much pain that I can’t hear. I am so dismayed that I can’t see.
public_domain_references.asv: Therefore are my loins filled with anguish; pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman in travail: I am pained so that I cannot hear; I am dismayed so that I cannot see.
public_domain_references.kjv: Therefore are my loins filled with pain: pangs have taken hold upon me, as the pangs of a woman that travaileth: I was bowed down at the hearing [of it;] I was dismayed at the seeing [of it].
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore are my loins filled with feebleness, and pangs have seized me as a travailing woman: I dealt wrongfully that I might not hear; I hasted that I might not see.

pob.text: My heart reels; shuddering terrifies me[a]. The twilight I longed for he has turned into terror for me.

spob.text: My heart reels, and shuddering fills me with terror. He has turned the twilight I longed for into terror for me.

public_domain_references.bsb: My heart falters; fear makes me tremble. The twilight of my desire has turned to horror.
public_domain_references.web: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
public_domain_references.asv: My heart fluttereth, horror hath affrighted me; the twilight that I desired hath been turned into trembling unto me.
public_domain_references.kjv: My heart panted, fearfulness affrighted me: the night of my pleasure hath he turned into fear unto me.
public_domain_references.brenton: My heart wanders, and transgression overwhelms me; my soul is occupied with fear.

pob.text: They set the table[a], they spread the rugs, they eat, they drink. Rise up, princes[b]; oil the shield.

spob.text: They prepare the table[a] and spread the rugs. They eat and drink. Princes, get up! Oil your shields for battle.[b]

public_domain_references.asv: They prepare the table, they set the watch, they eat, they drink: rise up, ye princes, anoint the shield.
public_domain_references.kjv: Prepare the table, watch in the watchtower, eat, drink: arise, ye princes, [and] anoint the shield.
public_domain_references.brenton: Prepare the table, eat, drink: arise, ye princes, and prepare [your] shields.

pob.text: For thus the Lord said to me: “Go[a], station the watchman; let him report what he sees.”

public_domain_references.brenton: For thus said the Lord to me, Go and station a watchman for thyself, and declare whatever thou shalt see.

public_domain_references.kjv: And he cried, A lion: My lord, I stand continually upon the watchtower in the daytime, and I am set in my ward whole nights:

pob.text: And look[a], here comes a chariot, a man with a pair of horsemen. And he answered and said, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon[c][b], and all the carved images of her gods he has shattered to the ground.”
