pob.text: For a people in Zion will dwell in Jerusalem[a]; you will surely weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; when he hears it[b], he will answer you.

spob.text: For the people of Zion will live in Jerusalem. You will weep no more. The LORD will certainly show you favor at the sound of your cry. As soon as he hears it, he will answer you.

public_domain_references.bsb: O people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious when you cry for help; when He hears, He will answer you.
public_domain_references.web: For the people will dwell in Zion at Jerusalem. You will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the voice of your cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.
public_domain_references.asv: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem; thou shalt weep no more; he will surely be gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear, he will answer thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the holy people shall dwell in Sion: and [whereas] Jerusalem has wept bitterly, [saying], Pity me; he shall pity thee: when he perceived the voice of thy cry, he hearkened to thee.

pob.text: And the Lord will give you bread of distress and water of oppression[a], yet your teacher will no longer hide himself[b], and your eyes will see your teacher.

spob.text: The Lord will give you bread and water marked by hardship and oppression.[a] Yet your teacher will no longer hide from you,[b] and you will see your teacher with your own eyes.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Lord will give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, but your Teacher will no longer hide Himself—with your own eyes you will see Him.
public_domain_references.web: Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teachers won’t be hidden any more, but your eyes will see your teachers;
public_domain_references.asv: And though the Lord give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be hidden anymore, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers;
public_domain_references.kjv: And [though] the Lord give you the bread of adversity, and the water of affliction, yet shall not thy teachers be removed into a corner any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers:
public_domain_references.brenton: And [though] the Lord shall give you the bread of affliction and scant water, yet they that cause thee to err shall no more at all draw nigh to thee; for thine eyes shall see those that cause thee to err,

pob.text: And your ears shall hear a word behind you[a], saying, “This is the way; walk in it,” when you turn to the right and when you turn to the left.

spob.text: Your ears will hear a word behind you: “This is the way. Walk in it.” You will hear it whenever you are about to turn right or left.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear this command behind you: “This is the way. Walk in it.”
public_domain_references.web: and when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
public_domain_references.asv: and thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it; when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
public_domain_references.kjv: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This [is] the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.
public_domain_references.brenton: and thine ears shall hear the words of them that went after thee to lead thee astray, who say, This [is] the way, let us walk in it, whether to the right or to the left.

pob.text: And you will defile the silver overlay of your carved idols and the gold plating of your cast images. You will scatter them like a menstrual cloth; you will say to them, “Go out!”

spob.text: You will treat as unclean the silver covering of your carved idols and the gold plating of your cast images. You will throw these coverings away like a menstrual cloth and say to them, “Get out!”

public_domain_references.bsb: So you will desecrate your silver-plated idols and your gold-plated images. You will throw them away like menstrual cloths, saying to them, “Be gone!”
public_domain_references.web: You shall defile the overlaying of your engraved images of silver, and the plating of your molten images of gold. You shall cast them away as an unclean thing. You shall tell it, “Go away!”
public_domain_references.asv: And ye shall defile the overlaying of thy graven images of silver, and the plating of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as an unclean thing; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence.
public_domain_references.brenton: And thou shalt pollute the plated idols, and thou shalt grind to powder the gilt ones, and shalt scatter them as the water of a removed [woman], and thou shalt thrust them forth as dung.

pob.text: And he will give rain for your seed with which you sow the ground[a], and bread from the produce of the ground; and it will be rich and plentiful[b]. On that day your livestock will graze in a broad pasture.

spob.text: He will send rain for the seed you plant in the ground. The harvest will provide you with rich, plentiful bread. On that day your livestock will graze in wide-open pastures.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then He will send rain for the seed that you have sown in the ground, and the food that comes from your land will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in open pastures.
public_domain_references.web: He will give the rain for your seed, with which you will sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground will be rich and plentiful. In that day, your livestock will feed in large pastures.
public_domain_references.asv: And he will give the rain for thy seed, wherewith thou shalt sow the ground; and bread of the increase of the ground, and it shall be fat and plenteous. In that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures;
public_domain_references.kjv: Then shall he give the rain of thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground withal; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then shall there be rain to the seed of thy land; and the bread of the fruit of thy land shall be plenteous and rich: and thy cattle shall feed in that day in a fertile and spacious place.

pob.text: And the oxen and the donkeys that work the ground will eat seasoned fodder[b][a], which has been winnowed with shovel and fork.

spob.text: The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat seasoned animal feed[a], winnowed with a shovel and fork.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat salted fodder, winnowed with shovel and pitchfork.
public_domain_references.web: The oxen likewise and the young donkeys that till the ground will eat savory feed, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
public_domain_references.asv: the oxen likewise and the young asses that till the ground shall eat savory provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.
public_domain_references.kjv: The oxen likewise and the young asses that ear the ground shall eat clean provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan.
public_domain_references.brenton: Your bulls and your oxen that till the ground, shall eat chaff mixed with winnowed barley.

pob.text: And on every high mountain and on every lofty hill there will be streams[a], channels of water, on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.

spob.text: On every high mountain and every lofty hill, there will be streams and channels of water[a]. This will happen on the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.

public_domain_references.bsb: And from every high mountain and every raised hill, streams of water will flow in the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall.
public_domain_references.web: There will be brooks and streams of water on every lofty mountain and on every high hill in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
public_domain_references.asv: And there shall be upon every lofty mountain, and upon every high hill, brooks [and] streams of waters, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
public_domain_references.kjv: And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, rivers [and] streams of waters in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.
public_domain_references.brenton: And there shall be upon every lofty mountain and upon every high hill, water running in that day, when many shall perish, and when the towers shall fall.

pob.text: And the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun[a], and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of seven days, on the day when Yahweh binds up the fracture of his people and heals the wound from his blow.

spob.text: The moon will shine as brightly as the sun. The sun’s light will be seven times as bright, like the light of seven days. This will happen on the day when Yahweh bandages his people’s fractures and heals the wound caused by his blow.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The light of the moon will be as bright as the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter—like the light of seven days—on the day that the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wounds He has inflicted.
public_domain_references.web: Moreover the light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, in the day that Yahweh binds up the fracture of his people, and heals the wound they were struck with.
public_domain_references.asv: Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that Jehovah bindeth up the hurt of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.
public_domain_references.kjv: Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold in the day when the Lord shall heal the breach of his people, and shall heal the pain of thy wound.

pob.text: Look[a], the name of Yahweh comes from afar, burning with his anger, and with dense smoke; his lips are full of wrath, and his tongue is like a consuming fire.

spob.text: Look! The name of Yahweh is coming from far away. His anger burns, and dense smoke rises.[a] His lips are full of wrath, and his tongue is like a fire that devours.

public_domain_references.bsb: Behold, the Name of the LORD comes from afar, with burning anger and dense smoke. His lips are full of fury, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, Yahweh’s name comes from far away, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of indignation. His tongue is as a devouring fire.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, the name of Jehovah cometh from far, burning with his anger, and in thick rising smoke: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue is as a devouring fire;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Behold, the name of the LORD cometh from far, burning [with] his anger, and the burden [thereof is] heavy: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire:
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold, the name of the Lord comes after a [long] time, burning wrath: the word of his lips is with glory, a word full of anger, and the anger of his wrath shall devour as fire.

pob.text: and his breath is like an overflowing stream[a]; it reaches up to the neck, to sift nations with a sieve of emptiness[c][b], and a misleading bridle is on the jaws of the peoples.

spob.text: His breath is like a flooding stream that rises to the neck. It sifts the nations with a sieve of emptiness[a]. A bridle on the jaws of the peoples leads them astray.

public_domain_references.bsb: His breath is like a rushing torrent that rises to the neck. He comes to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction; He bridles the jaws of the peoples to lead them astray.
public_domain_references.web: His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches even to the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction. A bridle that leads to ruin will be in the jaws of the peoples.
public_domain_references.asv: and his breath is as an overflowing stream, that reacheth even unto the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of destruction: and a bridle that causeth to err [shall be] in the jaws of the peoples.
public_domain_references.kjv: And his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and [there shall be] a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing [them] to err.
public_domain_references.brenton: And his breath, as rushing water in a valley, shall reach as far as the neck, and be divided, to confound the nations for [their] vain error: error also shall pursue them, and overtake them.

pob.text: The song will be for you as in the night when a feast is consecrated[a], and gladness of heart as when one goes with the flute to come to the mountain of Yahweh[d][c][b], to the Rock of Israel.

spob.text: You will sing as on the night when a feast is set apart as holy. Your hearts will be glad like people walking with flutes as they go to Yahweh’s mountain—to the Rock of Israel.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: You will sing as on the night of a holy festival, and your heart will rejoice like one who walks to the music of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
public_domain_references.web: You will have a song, as in the night when a holy feast is kept, and gladness of heart, as when one goes with a flute to come to Yahweh’s mountain, to Israel’s Rock.
public_domain_references.asv: Ye shall have a song as in the night when a holy feast is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come unto the mountain of Jehovah, to the Rock of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ye shall have a song, as in the night [when] a holy solemnity is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come into the mountain of the LORD, to the mighty One of Israel.
public_domain_references.brenton: Must ye always rejoice, and go into my holy places continually, as they that keep a feast? and must ye go with a pipe, as those that rejoice, into the mountain of the Lord, to the God of Israel?

pob.text: And Yahweh will make the majesty of his voice heard[a], and will show the descending blow of his arm, in furious anger and a flame of consuming fire[b], with cloudburst and storm and hailstones.

spob.text: Yahweh will make his majestic voice heard. He will show his arm coming down to strike,[a] in furious anger, with a flame of consuming fire, a violent cloudburst, a storm, and hailstones.

public_domain_references.bsb: And the LORD will cause His majestic voice to be heard and His mighty arm to be revealed, striking in angry wrath with a flame of consuming fire, and with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the descent of his arm, with the indignation of his anger and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
public_domain_references.asv: And Jehovah will cause his glorious voice to be heard, and will show the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of [his] anger, and the flame of a devouring fire, with a blast, and tempest, and hailstones.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the LORD shall cause his glorious voice to be heard, and shall shew the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of [his] anger, and [with] the flame of a devouring fire, [with] scattering, and tempest, and hailstones.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Lord shall make his glorious voice to be heard, and the wrath of his arm, to make a display with wrath and anger and devouring flame: he shall lighten terribly, and [his wrath shall be] as water and violent hail.

pob.text: For at the voice of Yahweh Assyria will be shattered[b][a]; with a rod he will strike.

spob.text: For Assyria will be shattered at the sound of Yahweh’s voice.[a] Yahweh will strike it with a rod.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: For Assyria will be shattered at the voice of the LORD; He will strike them with His scepter.
public_domain_references.web: For through Yahweh’s voice the Assyrian will be dismayed. He will strike him with his rod.
public_domain_references.asv: For through the voice of Jehovah shall the Assyrian be dismayed; with his rod will he smite [him].
public_domain_references.kjv: For through the voice of the LORD shall the Assyrian be beaten down, [which] smote with a rod.
public_domain_references.brenton: For by the voice of the Lord the Assyrians shall be overcome, [even] by the stroke wherewith he shall smite them.

pob.text: And every stroke of the appointed rod that Yahweh lays on him will be with tambourines and lyres[b][a]; and with battles of brandishing he will fight against them.

spob.text: Every blow from the rod Yahweh appointed for punishment and lays on him will be accompanied by tambourines and lyres.[a] Yahweh will fight against them in battles with sweeping movements.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: And with every stroke of the rod of punishment that the LORD brings down on them, the tambourines and lyres will sound as He battles with weapons brandished.
public_domain_references.web: Every stroke of the rod of punishment, which Yahweh will lay on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.
public_domain_references.asv: And every stroke of the appointed staff, which Jehovah shall lay upon him, shall be with [the sound of] tabrets and harps; and in battles with the brandishing [of his arm] will he fight with them.
public_domain_references.kjv: And [in] every place where the grounded staff shall pass, which the LORD shall lay upon him, [it] shall be with tabrets and harps: and in battles of shaking will he fight with it.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it shall happen to him from every side, [that] they from whom their hope of assistance was, in which he trusted, themselves shall war against him in turn with drums and with harp.

pob.text: For Topheth has long been prepared[a]; indeed, it is made ready for the king. He has made it deep and wide, with a pyre of fire and wood in abundance. The breath of Yahweh, like a stream of sulfur[c][b], kindles it.

spob.text: For Topheth[a] was prepared long ago; it is ready for the king. It has been made deep and wide. Its burning pile has plenty of fire and wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, sets it ablaze.

public_domain_references.bsb: For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its funeral pyre is deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a torrent of burning sulfur, sets it ablaze.
public_domain_references.web: For his burning place has long been ready. Yes, it is prepared for the king. He has made its pyre deep and large with fire and much wood. Yahweh’s breath, like a stream of sulfur, kindles it.
public_domain_references.asv: For a Topheth is prepared of old; yea, for the king it is made ready; he hath made it deep and large; the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of Jehovah, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.
public_domain_references.kjv: For Tophet [is] ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made [it] deep [and] large: the pile thereof [is] fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.
public_domain_references.brenton: For thou shalt be required before [thy] time: has it been prepared for thee also to reign? nay, God has [prepared for thee] a deep trench, wood piled, fire and much wood: the wrath of the Lord [shall be] as a trench kindled with sulphur.

pob.text: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help[a], who rely on horses and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong[c][b], but do not look to the Holy One of Israel and do not seek Yahweh.

spob.text: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help! They rely on horses. They trust in chariots because there are so many, and in horsemen because they are very strong. But they do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek Yahweh.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in their abundance of chariots and in their multitude of horsemen. They do not look to the Holy One of Israel; they do not seek the LORD.
public_domain_references.web: Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they don’t look to the Holy One of Israel, and they don’t seek Yahweh!
public_domain_references.asv: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, and rely on horses, and trust in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very strong, but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek Jehovah!
public_domain_references.kjv: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because [they are] many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the LORD!
public_domain_references.brenton: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, who trust in horses and chariots, for they are many; and in horses, [which are] a great multitude; and have not trusted in the Holy One of Israel, and have not sought the Lord.

pob.text: Yet he too is wise and brings disaster[a]; he does not take back his words[c][b], but rises against the house of evildoers and against the help of workers of iniquity.

spob.text: Yet the LORD is wise too, and he brings disaster.[a] He does not take back what he has said. He rises against the household of those who do evil and against the help supplied by those who practice wickedness.

public_domain_references.bsb: Yet He too is wise and brings disaster; He does not call back His words. He will rise up against the house of the wicked and against the allies of evildoers.
public_domain_references.web: Yet he also is wise, and will bring disaster, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of those who work iniquity.
public_domain_references.asv: Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words, but will arise against the house of the evil-doers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yet he also [is] wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity.
public_domain_references.brenton: Therefore he has wisely brought evils upon them, and his word shall not be frustrated; and he shall rise up against the houses of wicked men, and against their vain hope,

pob.text: Egypt is man and not God[a], and their horses are flesh and not spirit. When Yahweh stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble and the one helped will fall[c][b], and together all of them will come to an end.

spob.text: Egypt is only human, not God. Its horses are flesh, not spirit.[a] When Yahweh reaches out his hand to act against them, the helper will stumble, and those who receive its help will fall. All of them will come to an end together.

public_domain_references.bsb: But the Egyptians are men, not God; their horses are flesh, not spirit. When the LORD stretches out His hand, the helper will stumble, and the one he helps will fall; both will perish together.
public_domain_references.web: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When Yahweh stretches out his hand, both he who helps shall stumble, and he who is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.
public_domain_references.asv: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit: and when Jehovah shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall stumble, and he that is helped shall fall, and they all shall be consumed together.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now the Egyptians [are] men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.
public_domain_references.brenton: [even] an Egyptian, a man, and not God; the flesh of horses, and there is no help [in them]: but the Lord shall bring his hand upon them, and the helpers shall fail, and all shall perish together.

pob.text: For thus Yahweh said to me: As the lion or the young lion growls over its prey[a], and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their voice or cowed by their noise[b], so Yahweh of hosts will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.

spob.text:
This is what Yahweh said to me:

“A lion or a young lion growls over its prey.[a] Even when a whole group of shepherds is called together against it, their shouts do not frighten it, and their uproar does not intimidate it.[b] In the same way, Yahweh of hosts will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and its hill.”

public_domain_references.bsb: For this is what the LORD has said to me: “Like a lion roaring or a young lion over its prey— and though a band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or subdued by their clamor— so the LORD of Hosts will come down to do battle on Mount Zion and its heights.
public_domain_references.web: For Yahweh says to me, “As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds is called together against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for their noise, so Yahweh of Armies will come down to fight on Mount Zion and on its heights.
public_domain_references.asv: For thus saith Jehovah unto me, As the lion and the young lion growling over his prey, if a multitude of shepherds be called forth against him, will not be dismayed at their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so will Jehovah of hosts come down to fight upon mount Zion, and upon the hill thereof.
public_domain_references.kjv: For thus hath the LORD spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, [he] will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the LORD of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof.
public_domain_references.brenton: For thus said the Lord to me, As a lion would roar, or a lion's whelp over prey which he has taken, and cry over it, until the mountains are filled with his voice, and [the animals] are awe-struck and tremble at the fierceness of his wrath: so the Lord of hosts shall descend to fight upon the mount Sion, [even] upon her mountains.

pob.text: Like birds hovering[a], so Yahweh of Armies will shield Jerusalem—shielding and delivering, passing over and rescuing.

spob.text: Like birds hovering overhead, Yahweh of Armies will shield Jerusalem. He will shield and deliver it; he will pass over it[a] and rescue it.

public_domain_references.bsb: Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Hosts will protect Jerusalem. He will shield it and deliver it; He will pass over it and preserve it.”
public_domain_references.web: As birds hovering, so Yahweh of Armies will protect Jerusalem. He will protect and deliver it. He will pass over and preserve it.”
public_domain_references.asv: As birds hovering, so will Jehovah of hosts protect Jerusalem; he will protect and deliver [it], he will pass over and preserve [it].
public_domain_references.kjv: As birds flying, so will the LORD of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver [it; and] passing over he will preserve it.
public_domain_references.brenton: As birds flying, so shall the Lord of hosts defend; he shall defend Jerusalem, and he shall rescue, and save and deliver.

pob.text: Return to him from whom the sons of Israel have deeply revolted[a][b].

spob.text: Sons of Israel, return to the one from whom you have deeply rebelled.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Return to the One against whom you have so blatantly rebelled, O children of Israel.
public_domain_references.web: Return to him from whom you have deeply revolted, children of Israel.
public_domain_references.asv: Turn ye unto him from whom ye have deeply revolted, O children of Israel.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Turn ye unto [him from] whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted.
public_domain_references.brenton: Turn, ye children of Israel, who devise a deep and sinful counsel.

pob.text: For on that day each man will reject his idols of silver and his idols of gold, which your hands have made for you as sin.

spob.text: For on that day, every one of you will reject the silver and gold idols that your own hands made for yourselves—an act of sin.

public_domain_references.bsb: For on that day, every one of you will reject the idols of silver and gold that your own hands have sinfully made.
public_domain_references.web: For in that day everyone shall cast away his idols of silver and his idols of gold—sin which your own hands have made for you.
public_domain_references.asv: For in that day they shall cast away every man his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin.
public_domain_references.kjv: For in that day every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you [for] a sin.
public_domain_references.brenton: For in that day men shall renounce their silver idols and [their] golden idols, which their hands made.

pob.text: And Assyria will fall by a sword not of man[a], and a sword not of humankind will devour him; and he will flee from before the sword[d][c][b], and his young men will become forced labor.

spob.text: Assyria will fall by a sword no man wields; a sword no human being wields will devour it. Assyria will flee from the sword, and its young men will be forced into labor.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: “Then Assyria will fall, but not by the sword of man; a sword will devour them, but not one made by mortals. They will flee before the sword, and their young men will be put to forced labor.
public_domain_references.web: “The Assyrian will fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of mankind, shall devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will become subject to forced labor.
public_domain_references.asv: And the Assyrian shall fall by the sword, not of man; and the sword, not of men, shall devour him; and he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall become subject to taskwork.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall be discomfited.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Assyrian shall fall: not the sword of a great man, nor the sword of a mean man shall devour him; neither shall he flee from the face of the sword: but the young men shall be overthrown:

pob.text: His rock will pass away because of terror[a], and his princes will be terrified at the signal, declares Yahweh[c][b], whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.

spob.text: “Assyria’s rock[a] will vanish because of terror, and its leaders will panic at the battle signal,” declares Yahweh, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Their rock will pass away for fear, and their princes will panic at the sight of the battle standard,” declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: His rock will pass away by reason of terror, and his princes will be afraid of the banner,” says Yahweh, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.asv: And his rock shall pass away by reason of terror, and his princes shall be dismayed at the ensign, saith Jehovah, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he shall pass over to his strong hold for fear, and his princes shall be afraid of the ensign, saith the LORD, whose fire [is] in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.brenton: for they shall be compassed with rocks as with a trench, and shall be worsted; and he that flees shall be taken. Thus saith the Lord, Blessed is he that has a seed in Sion, and household friends in Jerusalem.

pob.text: Behold[a], a king will reign in righteousness[d][c][b], and princes will rule with justice.

spob.text: Look! A king will rule according to what is right, and rulers will govern with justice.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule with justice.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in justice.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment.
public_domain_references.brenton: For, behold, a righteous king shall reign, and princes shall govern with judgment.

pob.text: And a man will be like a hiding place from the wind[a], and a shelter from the storm, like streams of water in a dry place[c][b], like the shade of a massive rock in a weary land.

spob.text: A man will be like a refuge from the wind and a shelter from the storm, like streams of water in a dry place and like the shade of a massive rock in a land that leaves people weary.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Each will be like a shelter from the wind, a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shadow of a great rock in an arid land.
public_domain_references.web: A man shall be as a hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the storm, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a large rock in a weary land.
public_domain_references.asv: And a man shall be as a hiding-place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest, as streams of water in a dry place, as the shade of a great rock in a weary land.
public_domain_references.kjv: And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.
public_domain_references.brenton: And a man shall hide his words, and be hidden, as from rushing water, and shall appear in Sion as a rushing river, glorious in a thirsty land.

pob.text: Then the eyes of those who see will not be dim[a], and the ears of those who hear will listen attentively.

spob.text: Then those who see will no longer have dim eyes, and those who hear will listen carefully.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
public_domain_references.web: The eyes of those who see will not be dim, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
public_domain_references.asv: And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they shall no more trust in men, but they shall incline their ears to hear.

pob.text: The heart of the hasty will understand knowledge[b][a], and the tongue of stammerers will hasten to speak clearly.

spob.text: The hearts of rash people will gain knowledge and understanding. Those with stammering tongues will quickly speak clearly.

public_domain_references.bsb: The mind of the rash will know and understand, and the stammering tongue will speak clearly and fluently.
public_domain_references.web: The heart of the rash will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers will be ready to speak plainly.
public_domain_references.asv: And the heart of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.
public_domain_references.kjv: The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the heart of the weak ones shall attend to hear, and the stammering tongues shall soon learn to speak peace.

pob.text: No longer will the fool be called noble[d][c][b][a], nor will the scoundrel be called generous.

spob.text: People will no longer call a morally corrupt fool noble or call a scoundrel generous.

public_domain_references.bsb: No longer will a fool be called noble, nor a scoundrel be respected.
public_domain_references.web: The fool will no longer be called noble, nor the scoundrel be highly respected.
public_domain_references.asv: The fool shall be no more called noble, nor the churl said to be bountiful.
public_domain_references.kjv: The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said [to be] bountiful.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they shall no more at all tell a fool to rule, and thy servants shall no more at all say, Be silent.

pob.text: For a fool speaks folly[a], and his heart devises iniquity: to practice godlessness and to speak error against Yahweh[c][b], to leave the hungry person empty and to withhold drink from the thirsty.

spob.text: For a fool speaks foolish and disgraceful things. His heart produces evil: he lives without regard for God and speaks falsehood against Yahweh.[a] He leaves hungry people with nothing to eat and keeps the thirsty from getting anything to drink.

public_domain_references.bsb: For a fool speaks foolishness; his mind plots iniquity. He practices ungodliness and speaks falsely about the LORD; he leaves the hungry empty and deprives the thirsty of drink.
public_domain_references.web: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practice profanity, and to utter error against Yahweh, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
public_domain_references.asv: For the fool will speak folly, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise profaneness, and to utter error against Jehovah, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the vile person will speak villany, and his heart will work iniquity, to practise hypocrisy, and to utter error against the LORD, to make empty the soul of the hungry, and he will cause the drink of the thirsty to fail.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the fool shall speak foolish words, and his heart shall meditate vanities, and to perform lawless deeds and to speak error against the Lord, to scatter hungry souls, and he will cause the thirsty souls to be empty.

pob.text: And the rogue’s devices are evil[a]; he devises schemes to ruin the humble with lying words[c][b], even when the poor man speaks what is just.

spob.text: A rogue’s methods are evil.[a] He makes plans to ruin humble people with lies, even when a poor man speaks what is right.

public_domain_references.bsb: The weapons of the scoundrel are destructive; he hatches plots to destroy the poor with lies, even when the plea of the needy is just.
public_domain_references.web: The ways of the scoundrel are evil. He devises wicked plans to destroy the humble with lying words, even when the needy speaks right.
public_domain_references.asv: And the instruments of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the meek with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.
public_domain_references.kjv: The instruments also of the churl [are] evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the counsel of the wicked will devise iniquity, to destroy the poor with unjust words, and ruin the cause of the poor in judgment.

pob.text: But a noble man plans noble things[b][a], and he stands on noble things.

spob.text: But a noble man plans what is noble,[a] and he stands firm in what is noble.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: But a noble man makes honorable plans; he stands up for worthy causes.
public_domain_references.web: But the noble devises noble things, and he will continue in noble things.
public_domain_references.asv: But the noble deviseth noble things; and in noble things shall he continue.
public_domain_references.kjv: But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand.
public_domain_references.brenton: But the godly have devised wise [measures], and this counsel shall stand.

pob.text: You complacent women[a], rise up; hear my voice. You confident daughters[c][b], listen to my word.

spob.text: Get up, you women who are too comfortable and unconcerned; listen to me. You daughters[a] who feel safe and self-assured, pay attention to what I say.

public_domain_references.bsb: Stand up, you complacent women; listen to me. Give ear to my word, you overconfident daughters.
public_domain_references.web: Rise up, you women who are at ease! Hear my voice! You careless daughters, give ear to my speech!
public_domain_references.asv: Rise up, ye women that are at ease, [and] hear my voice; ye careless daughters, give ear unto my speech.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Rise up, ye women that are at ease; hear my voice, ye careless daughters; give ear unto my speech.
public_domain_references.brenton: Rise up, ye rich women, and hear my voice; ye confident daughters, hearken to my words.

pob.text: In little more than a year you will tremble[a], you complacent women, because the grape harvest will fail[c][b]; the fruit harvest will not come.

spob.text: You complacent women,[a] in just over a year you will tremble. This will happen because the grape harvest will fail, and the fruit harvest[b] will not come.

public_domain_references.bsb: In a little more than a year you will tremble, O secure ones. For the grape harvest will fail and the fruit harvest will not arrive.
public_domain_references.web: For days beyond a year you will be troubled, you careless women; for the vintage will fail. The harvest won’t come.
public_domain_references.asv: For days beyond a year shall ye be troubled, ye careless women; for the vintage shall fail, the ingathering shall not come.
public_domain_references.kjv: Many days and years shall ye be troubled, ye careless women: for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come.
public_domain_references.brenton: Remember for a full year in pain, yet with hope: the vintage has been cut off, it has ceased, it shall by no means come again.

pob.text: Tremble[a], you complacent women; shudder, you confident ones. Strip, make yourselves bare[c][b], and tie sackcloth around your waist.

spob.text: Tremble, you complacent women! Shudder, you women who feel secure! Strip off your clothes and make yourselves bare. Tie sackcloth around your waist.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Shudder, you ladies of leisure; tremble, you daughters of complacency. Strip yourselves bare and put sackcloth around your waists.
public_domain_references.web: Tremble, you women who are at ease! Be troubled, you careless ones! Strip yourselves, make yourselves naked, and put sackcloth on your waist.
public_domain_references.asv: Tremble, ye women that are at ease; be troubled, ye careless ones; strip you, and make you bare, and gird [sackcloth] upon your loins.
public_domain_references.kjv: Tremble, ye women that are at ease; be troubled, ye careless ones: strip you, and make you bare, and gird [sackcloth] upon [your] loins.
public_domain_references.brenton: Be amazed, be pained, ye confident ones: strip you, bare yourselves, gird your loins;

pob.text: They beat their breasts in mourning over the delightful fields[b][a], over the fruitful vine.

spob.text: They mourn for the pleasant fields and the fruitful vine, beating their breasts in grief.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vines,
public_domain_references.web: Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
public_domain_references.asv: They shall smite upon the breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
public_domain_references.kjv: They shall lament for the teats, for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine.
public_domain_references.brenton: and beat on your breasts, because of the pleasant field, and the fruit of the vine.

pob.text: On the land of my people[a], thorn and brier will come up; indeed[b], over all the joyful houses in the exultant city.

spob.text: Thorns and briers will grow on my people’s land, even over all the joyful houses in the rejoicing city.

public_domain_references.bsb: and for the land of my people, overgrown with thorns and briers— even for every house of merriment in this city of revelry.
public_domain_references.web: Thorns and briers will come up on my people’s land; yes, on all the houses of joy in the joyous city.
public_domain_references.asv: Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers; yea, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city.
public_domain_references.kjv: Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns [and] briers; yea, upon all the houses of joy [in] the joyous city:
public_domain_references.brenton: [As for] the land of my people, the thorn and grass shall come upon [it], and joy shall be removed from every house.

pob.text: For the palace is abandoned[a], the crowded city is forsaken; Ophel and the watchtower have become caves forever, a joy for wild donkeys[c][b], a pasture for flocks.

spob.text: The palace is deserted, and the city, once full of people, has been abandoned. Ophel[a] and the watchtower have become caves forever,[b] a delight for wild donkeys and grazing land for flocks.

public_domain_references.bsb: For the palace will be forsaken, the busy city abandoned. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever— the delight of wild donkeys and a pasture for flocks—
public_domain_references.web: For the palace will be forsaken. The populous city will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens forever, a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks,
public_domain_references.asv: For the palace shall be forsaken; the populous city shall be deserted; the hill and the watch-tower shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;
public_domain_references.kjv: Because the palaces shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; the forts and towers shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;
public_domain_references.brenton: [As for] the rich city, the houses are deserted; they shall abandon the wealth of the city, [and] the pleasant houses: and the villages shall be caves for ever, the joy of wild asses, shepherds' pastures;

pob.text: until a spirit from on high is poured out on us[a], and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field[b], and the fruitful field is regarded as a forest.

spob.text: until a spirit from above is poured out on us.[a] Then the wilderness will become fruitful land,[b] and the fruitful land will be regarded as a forest.

public_domain_references.bsb: until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the desert will be an orchard, and the orchard will seem like a forest.
public_domain_references.web: until the Spirit is poured on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a forest.
public_domain_references.asv: until the Spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness become a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be esteemed as a forest.
public_domain_references.kjv: Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest.
public_domain_references.brenton: until the Spirit shall come upon you from on high, and Chermel shall be desert, and Chermel shall be counted for a forest.

pob.text: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness[b][a], and righteousness will abide in the fruitful field.

spob.text: Then justice will make its home in the wilderness, and righteousness will live in the fertile fields.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then justice will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field.
public_domain_references.web: Then justice will dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness will remain in the fruitful field.
public_domain_references.asv: Then justice shall dwell in the wilderness; and righteousness shall abide in the fruitful field.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then judgment shall dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness remain in the fruitful field.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then judgment shall abide in the wilderness, and righteousness shall dwell in Carmel.

pob.text: And the work of righteousness will be peace, and the service of righteousness, quietness and security forever.

spob.text: Righteousness at work will bring peace. The service of righteousness will bring quietness and security forever.

public_domain_references.bsb: The work of righteousness will be peace; the service of righteousness will be quiet confidence forever.
public_domain_references.web: The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence forever.
public_domain_references.asv: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness, quietness and confidence for ever.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the works of righteousness shall be peace; and righteousness shall ensure rest, and [the righteous] shall be confident for ever.

pob.text: And my people will dwell in a peaceful habitation[a], in secure dwellings[b], and in quiet resting places.

spob.text: My people will live in peaceful homes, in safe dwellings, and in quiet places of rest.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
public_domain_references.web: My people will live in a peaceful habitation, in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting places,
public_domain_references.asv: And my people shall abide in a peaceable habitation, and in safe dwellings, and in quiet resting-places.
public_domain_references.kjv: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places;
public_domain_references.brenton: And his people shall inhabit a city of peace, and dwell in [it] in confidence, and they shall rest with wealth.

pob.text: And it will hail when the forest falls[a], and the city will be utterly laid low in the lowland.

spob.text: It will hail when the forest falls,[a] and in the lowland the city will be completely brought down.

public_domain_references.bsb: But hail will level the forest, and the city will sink to the depths.
public_domain_references.web: though hail flattens the forest, and the city is leveled completely.
public_domain_references.asv: But it shall hail in the downfall of the forest; and the city shall be utterly laid low.
public_domain_references.kjv: When it shall hail, coming down on the forest; and the city shall be low in a low place.
public_domain_references.brenton: And if the hail should come down, it shall not come upon you; and they that dwell in the forests shall be in confidence, as those in the plain country.

pob.text: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters[a], who let the feet of the ox and the donkey range free.

spob.text: Blessed are you who plant seed wherever there is water and let the ox and donkey roam freely.

public_domain_references.bsb: Blessed are those who sow beside abundant waters, who let the ox and donkey range freely.
public_domain_references.web: Blessed are you who sow beside all waters, who send out the feet of the ox and the donkey.
public_domain_references.asv: Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth the feet of the ox and the ass.
public_domain_references.kjv: Blessed [are] ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth [thither] the feet of the ox and the ass.
public_domain_references.brenton: Blessed are they that sow by every water, where the ox and ass tread.

pob.text: Woe to you[a], destroyer, though you yourself have not been destroyed, and betrayer, though they have not betrayed you. When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed; when you cease betraying[c][b], they will betray you.

spob.text: Woe to you! You destroy others, but you have not been destroyed. You betray others, but you have not been betrayed.[a] When you finish destroying, you will be destroyed.[b] When you stop betraying, others will betray you.

public_domain_references.bsb: Woe to you, O destroyer never destroyed, O traitor never betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed. When you have finished betraying, you will be betrayed.
public_domain_references.web: Woe to you who destroy, but you weren’t destroyed, and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have finished betrayal, you will be betrayed.
public_domain_references.asv: Woe to thee that destroyest, and thou wast not destroyed; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! When thou hast ceased to destroy, thou shalt be destroyed; and when thou hast made an end of dealing treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.
public_domain_references.kjv: Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou [wast] not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; [and] when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee.
public_domain_references.brenton: Woe to them that afflict you; but no one makes you miserable: and he that deals perfidiously with you does not deal perfidiously: they that deal perfidiously shall be taken and given up, and as a moth on a garment, so shall they be spoiled.

pob.text: O Yahweh[a], be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be our arm every morning, also our salvation in the time of distress.

spob.text: Yahweh, show us grace; we wait for you. Be their strength every morning,[a] and be our salvation when we are in trouble.

public_domain_references.bsb: O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our strength every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
public_domain_references.asv: O Jehovah, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou our arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
public_domain_references.kjv: O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble.
public_domain_references.brenton: Lord, have mercy upon us; for we have trusted in thee: the seed of the rebellious is gone to destruction, but our deliverance was in a time of affliction.

pob.text: At the sound of the tumult[a], peoples fled; at your rising up[b], nations were scattered.

spob.text: At the sound of the uproar, peoples fled. When you rose to act,[a] nations scattered.

public_domain_references.bsb: The peoples flee the thunder of Your voice; the nations scatter when You rise.
public_domain_references.web: At the noise of the thunder, the peoples have fled. When you lift yourself up, the nations are scattered.
public_domain_references.asv: At the noise of the tumult the peoples are fled; at the lifting up of thyself the nations are scattered.
public_domain_references.kjv: At the noise of the tumult the people fled; at the lifting up of thyself the nations were scattered.
public_domain_references.brenton: By reason of the terrible sound the nations were dismayed for fear of thee, and the heathen were scattered.

pob.text: And your spoil will be gathered like the gathering of locusts[a]; like the rushing of swarms[b], they rush upon it.

spob.text: Your war plunder will be gathered up the way locusts gather. They rush upon it like swarms.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Your spoil, O nations, is gathered as by locusts; like a swarm of locusts men sweep over it.
public_domain_references.web: Your plunder will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.
public_domain_references.asv: And your spoil shall be gathered as the caterpillar gathereth: as locusts leap shall men leap upon it.
public_domain_references.kjv: And your spoil shall be gathered [like] the gathering of the caterpiller: as the running to and fro of locusts shall he run upon them.
public_domain_references.brenton: And now shall the spoils of your small and great be gathered: as if one should gather locusts, so shall they mock you.

pob.text: Yahweh is exalted[a], for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.

spob.text: Yahweh is exalted because he lives in the heights. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.

public_domain_references.bsb: The LORD is exalted, for He dwells on high; He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
public_domain_references.web: Yahweh is exalted, for he dwells on high. He has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
public_domain_references.asv: Jehovah is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
public_domain_references.kjv: The LORD is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.
public_domain_references.brenton: The God who dwells on high is holy: Sion is filled with judgment and righteousness.

pob.text: And he will be the stability of your times[a], a wealth of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge[c][b]; the fear of Yahweh is his treasure.

spob.text: He will make your times secure and provide abundant salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. Reverent fear of Yahweh is his treasure.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: He will be the sure foundation for your times, a storehouse of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion’s treasure.
public_domain_references.web: There will be stability in your times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. The fear of Yahweh is your treasure.
public_domain_references.asv: And there shall be stability in thy times, abundance of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge: the fear of Jehovah is thy treasure.
public_domain_references.kjv: And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, [and] strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD [is] his treasure.
public_domain_references.brenton: They shall be delivered up to the law: our salvation is our treasure: there are wisdom and knowledge and piety toward the Lord; these are the treasures of righteousness.

pob.text: Look[a], their heroes cry out outside[b]; the messengers of peace weep bitterly.

public_domain_references.web: Behold, their valiant ones cry outside; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, their valiant ones cry without; the ambassadors of peace weep bitterly.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, their valiant ones shall cry without: the ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold now, these shall be terrified with fear of you: those whom ye feared shall cry out because of you: messengers shall be sent, bitterly weeping, entreating for peace.

spob.text: The highways are desolate, and travelers no longer use the roads. He has broken the covenant, treated the cities with contempt,[a] and has no regard for anyone.[b]

public_domain_references.kjv: The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: he hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the ways of these shall be made desolate: the terror of the nations has been made to cease, and the covenant with these is taken away, and ye shall by no means deem them men.

pob.text: The land mourns and withers[a]; Lebanon is ashamed and withers away. Sharon has become like the Arabah[b], and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

spob.text: The land mourns and dries up. Lebanon is put to shame and withers away. Sharon has become like a desert plain,[a] and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.

public_domain_references.kjv: The earth mourneth [and] languisheth: Lebanon is ashamed [and] hewn down: Sharon is like a wilderness; and Bashan and Carmel shake off [their fruits].
public_domain_references.brenton: The land mourns; Libanus is ashamed: Saron is become marshes; Galilee shall be laid bare, and Chermel.

pob.text: Now I will arise[a], says Yahweh; now I will be exalted; now I will lift myself up.

spob.text: “Now I will rise,” says Yahweh. “Now I will lift myself up. Now I will be exalted.”[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: “Now I will arise,” says the LORD. “Now I will lift Myself up. Now I will be exalted.
public_domain_references.web: “Now I will arise,” says Yahweh. “Now I will lift myself up. Now I will be exalted.
public_domain_references.asv: Now will I arise, saith Jehovah; now will I lift up myself; now will I be exalted.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now will I rise, saith the LORD; now will I be exalted; now will I lift up myself.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now will I arise, saith the Lord, now will I be glorified; now will I be exalted.

pob.text: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble[a]. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.

spob.text: What you conceive is chaff, and what you give birth to is straw. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will consume you.
public_domain_references.web: You will conceive chaff. You will give birth to stubble. Your breath is a fire that will devour you.
public_domain_references.asv: Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath is a fire that shall devour you.
public_domain_references.kjv: Ye shall conceive chaff, ye shall bring forth stubble: your breath, [as] fire, shall devour you.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now shall ye see, now shall ye perceive; the strength of your breath shall be vain; fire shall devour you.

pob.text: And the peoples will become burnings of lime; like cut thornbushes[a], they will be burned in the fire.

spob.text: The peoples will become like lime made by burning limestone. Like thornbushes that have been cut down, they will be burned in the fire.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The peoples will be burned to ashes, like thorns cut down and set ablaze.
public_domain_references.web: The peoples will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the fire.
public_domain_references.asv: And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime, as thorns cut down, that are burned in the fire.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the people shall be [as] the burnings of lime: [as] thorns cut up shall they be burned in the fire.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the nations shall be burnt up; as a thorn in the field cast out and burnt up.

pob.text: Hear[a], you who are far away, what I have done; and know, you who are near[b], my might.

spob.text: You who are far away, listen to what I have done. You who are near, know my power.

public_domain_references.bsb: You who are far off, hear what I have done; you who are near, acknowledge My might.”
public_domain_references.web: Hear, you who are far off, what I have done; and, you who are near, acknowledge my might.”
public_domain_references.asv: Hear, ye that are far off, what I have done; and, ye that are near, acknowledge my might.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Hear, ye [that are] far off, what I have done; and, ye [that are] near, acknowledge my might.
public_domain_references.brenton: They that are afar off shall hear what I have done; they that draw nigh shall know my strength.

pob.text: Sinners in Zion are afraid[d][c][b][a]; trembling has seized the godless: “Who among us can dwell with a consuming fire? Who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?”

spob.text: Sinners in Zion are filled with fear. Trembling grips the godless[a]: “Who among us can live with a fire that consumes[b]? Who among us can live with flames that burn forever?”

public_domain_references.web: The sinners in Zion are afraid. Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring fire? Who among us can live with everlasting burning?
public_domain_references.asv: The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling hath seized the godless ones: Who among us can dwell with the devouring fire? who among us can dwell with everlasting burnings?
public_domain_references.kjv: The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites. Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
public_domain_references.brenton: The sinners in Sion have departed; trembling shall seize the ungodly. Who will tell you that a fire is kindled? Who will tell you of the eternal place?

pob.text: He who walks in righteousness and speaks what is upright[a], who despises gain from extortions, who shakes his hands free from taking a bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed[c][b], and shuts his eyes from looking on evil—

public_domain_references.asv: He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from taking a bribe, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from looking upon evil:
public_domain_references.kjv: He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil;
public_domain_references.brenton: He that walks in righteousness, speaking rightly, hating transgression and iniquity, and shaking his hands from gifts, stopping his ears that he should not hear the judgment of blood, shutting his eyes that he should not see injustice;

pob.text: He will dwell on the heights[a]; rocky fortresses will be his refuge; his bread will be given[b], his water will be sure.

public_domain_references.asv: He shall dwell on high; his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks; his bread shall be given [him]; his waters shall be sure.
public_domain_references.kjv: He shall dwell on high: his place of defence [shall be] the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters [shall be] sure.

pob.text: Your eyes will behold the king in his beauty[a]; they will see a far-reaching land.

public_domain_references.bsb: Your eyes will see the King in His beauty and behold a land that stretches afar.
public_domain_references.web: Your eyes will see the king in his beauty. They will see a distant land.
public_domain_references.asv: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold a land that reacheth afar.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off.
public_domain_references.brenton: Ye shall see a king with glory: your eyes shall behold a land from afar.

pob.text: Your heart will meditate on terror: “Where is the scribe? Where is the one who weighs? Where is the one who counts the towers?”[a][b]

spob.text: In your heart, you will think back on the terror: “Where is the record-keeper? Where is the one who did the weighing? Where is the one who counted the towers?”[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Your mind will ponder the former terror: “Where is he who tallies? Where is he who weighs? Where is he who counts the towers?”
public_domain_references.web: Your heart will meditate on the terror. Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers?
public_domain_references.asv: Thy heart shall muse on the terror: Where is he that counted, where is he that weighed [the tribute]? where is he that counted the towers?
public_domain_references.kjv: Thine heart shall meditate terror. Where [is] the scribe? where [is] the receiver? where [is] he that counted the towers?
public_domain_references.brenton: Your soul shall meditate terror. Where are the scribes? where are the counsellors, where is he that numbers them that are growing up,

pob.text: You will no longer see the insolent people[a], a people of speech too deep to understand[c][b], of a stammering tongue without comprehension.

spob.text: You will no longer see those insolent people—a people whose foreign speech is too difficult for you to understand, whose words sound broken and make no sense to you.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: You will no longer see the insolent, a people whose speech is unintelligible, who stammer in a language you cannot understand.
public_domain_references.web: You will no longer see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that you can’t comprehend, with a strange language that you can’t understand.
public_domain_references.asv: Thou shalt not see the fierce people, a people of a deep speech that thou canst not comprehend, of a strange tongue that thou canst not understand.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thou shalt not see a fierce people, a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, [that thou canst] not understand.
public_domain_references.brenton: [even] the small and great people? with whom he took not counsel, neither did he understand [a people] of deep speech, so that a despised people should not hear, and there is no understanding to him that hears.

pob.text: Look upon Zion[a], the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that will not be moved; its stakes will never be pulled up[c][b], and none of its ropes will be torn apart.

spob.text: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals.[a] Your own eyes will see Jerusalem as a peaceful home—a tent that will never be moved. Its stakes will never be pulled up, and none of its ropes will break.

public_domain_references.bsb: Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not wander; its tent pegs will not be pulled up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
public_domain_references.web: Look at Zion, the city of our appointed festivals. Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a quiet habitation, a tent that won’t be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.
public_domain_references.asv: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tent that shall not be removed, the stakes whereof shall never be plucked up, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken.
public_domain_references.kjv: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities: thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tabernacle [that] shall not be taken down; not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold the city Sion, our refuge: thine eyes shall behold Jerusalem, a rich city, tabernacles which shall not be shaken, neither shall the pins of her tabernacle be moved for ever, neither shall her cords be at all broken:

pob.text: But there the majestic Yahweh will be for us a place of rivers[a], of broad streams, where no rowing ship can go[c][b], and no mighty vessel can pass through.

spob.text: But there the majestic Yahweh will be our place—a place of wide rivers and streams. No rowing ship can travel there, and no mighty vessel can pass through.

public_domain_references.bsb: But there the Majestic One, our LORD, will be for us a place of rivers and wide canals, where no galley with oars will row, and no majestic vessel will pass.
public_domain_references.web: But there Yahweh will be with us in majesty, a place of wide rivers and streams, in which no galley with oars will go, neither will any gallant ship pass by there.
public_domain_references.asv: But there Jehovah will be with us in majesty, a place of broad rivers and streams, wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ship pass thereby.
public_domain_references.kjv: But there the glorious LORD [will be] unto us a place of broad rivers [and] streams; wherein shall go no galley with oars, neither shall gallant ship pass thereby.
public_domain_references.brenton: for the name of the Lord is great to you: ye shall have a place, [even] rivers and wide and spacious channels: thou shalt not go this way, neither a vessel with oars go [thereby].

pob.text: For Yahweh is our judge[a]; Yahweh is our lawgiver; Yahweh is our king[b]; he will save us.

spob.text: For Yahweh is our judge. Yahweh gives us our laws. Yahweh is our king. He will save us.

public_domain_references.web: For Yahweh is our judge. Yahweh is our lawgiver. Yahweh is our king. He will save us.
public_domain_references.asv: For Jehovah is our judge, Jehovah is our lawgiver, Jehovah is our king; he will save us.
public_domain_references.kjv: For the LORD [is] our judge, the LORD [is] our lawgiver, the LORD [is] our king; he will save us.
public_domain_references.brenton: For my God is great: the Lord our judge shall not pass me by: the Lord is our prince, the Lord is our king; the Lord, he shall save us.

spob.text: Your ropes hang loose. They cannot firmly secure the base of the mast or spread the sail.[a] Then a great amount of plunder will be divided up.[b] Even people who are lame will carry off the spoil.

public_domain_references.bsb: Your ropes are slack; they cannot secure the mast or spread the sail. Then an abundance of spoils will be divided, and even the lame will carry off plunder.
public_domain_references.web: Your rigging is untied. They couldn’t strengthen the foot of their mast. They couldn’t spread the sail. Then the prey of a great plunder was divided. The lame took the prey.
public_domain_references.asv: Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not strengthen the foot of their mast, they could not spread the sail: then was the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame took the prey.
public_domain_references.kjv: Thy tacklings are loosed; they could not well strengthen their mast, they could not spread the sail: then is the prey of a great spoil divided; the lame take the prey.
public_domain_references.brenton: Thy cords are broken, for they had no strength: thy mast has given way, it shall not spread the sails, it shall not bear a signal, until it be given up for plunder; therefore shall many lame men take spoil.

public_domain_references.kjv: And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein [shall be] forgiven [their] iniquity.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the people dwelling among them shall by no means say, I am in pain: for their sin shall be forgiven them.

public_domain_references.brenton: Draw near, ye nations; and hearken, ye princes; let the earth hear, and they that are in it; the world, and the people that are therein.

public_domain_references.web: The wild oxen will come down with them, and the young bulls with the mighty bulls; and their land will be drunken with blood, and their dust made greasy with fat.
