spob.text: For Yahweh has a day of vengeance, a year of repayment for Zion’s case.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
public_domain_references.web: For Yahweh has a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
public_domain_references.asv: For Jehovah hath a day of vengeance, a year of recompense for the cause of Zion.
public_domain_references.kjv: For [it is] the day of the LORD’s vengeance, [and] the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.
public_domain_references.brenton: For it is the day of the judgment of the Lord, and the year of the recompence of Sion in judgment.

pob.text: Her wadis will be turned into pitch[a], and her dust into sulfur[b]; her land will become burning pitch.

spob.text: Her streambeds[a] will become pitch. Her dust will become sulfur, and her land will become burning pitch.

public_domain_references.bsb: Edom’s streams will be turned to tar, and her soil to sulfur; her land will become a blazing pitch.
public_domain_references.web: Its streams will be turned into pitch, its dust into sulfur, and its land will become burning pitch.
public_domain_references.asv: And the streams of [Edom] shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch.
public_domain_references.brenton: And her valleys shall be turned into pitch, and her land into sulphur; and her land shall be as pitch burning night and day;

pob.text: Night and day it shall not be quenched; its smoke shall go up forever[a]. From generation to generation it shall lie waste; forever and ever no one shall pass through it.

spob.text: The fire will not go out, night or day. Its smoke will rise forever. From one generation to the next, it will remain a wasteland. Forever and ever, no one will pass through it.

public_domain_references.bsb: It will not be quenched—day or night. Its smoke will ascend forever. From generation to generation it will lie desolate; no one will ever again pass through it.
public_domain_references.web: It won’t be quenched night or day. Its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation, it will lie waste. No one will pass through it forever and ever.
public_domain_references.asv: It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever; from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.
public_domain_references.kjv: It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever.
public_domain_references.brenton: and it shall never be quenched, and her smoke shall go up: it shall be made desolate throughout her generations,

pob.text: The desert owl and the hedgehog will possess her[a], and the owl and the raven will dwell in her[b]; he will stretch over her the measuring line of desolation and the plumb stones of emptiness.

spob.text: The desert owl and the hedgehog will take possession of the land.[a] The owl and the raven will live there. He will stretch a measuring line of desolation over it and use plumb stones of emptiness.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: The desert owl and screech owl will possess it, and the great owl and raven will dwell in it. The LORD will stretch out over Edom a measuring line of chaos and a plumb line of destruction.
public_domain_references.web: But the pelican and the porcupine will possess it. The owl and the raven will dwell in it. He will stretch the line of confusion over it, and the plumb line of emptiness.
public_domain_references.asv: But the pelican and the porcupine shall possess it; and the owl and the raven shall dwell therein: and he will stretch over it the line of confusion, and the plummet of emptiness.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it; the owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness.
public_domain_references.brenton: and for a long time birds and hedgehogs, and ibises and ravens shall dwell in it: and the measuring line of desolation shall be cast over it, and satyrs shall dwell in it.

pob.text: They will call its nobles[a], but there will be no kingdom there, and all its princes will be nothing.

spob.text: Its nobles will be called,[a] but no kingdom will exist there. Its princes will all be no more.

public_domain_references.bsb: No nobles will be left to proclaim a king, and all her princes will come to nothing.
public_domain_references.web: They shall call its nobles to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing.
public_domain_references.asv: They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there; and all its princes shall be nothing.
public_domain_references.kjv: They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none [shall be] there, and all her princes shall be nothing.
public_domain_references.brenton: Her princes shall be no more; for her kings and her great men shall be destroyed.

pob.text: Thorns will grow over her palaces[a], nettles and brambles in her fortresses; and she will become a haunt of jackals[b], a pasture for ostriches.

spob.text: Her palaces will be overgrown with thorns, and nettles and brambles will fill her fortresses. She will become a home for jackals and a pasture for ostriches.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Her towers will be overgrown with thorns, her fortresses with thistles and briers. She will become a haunt for jackals, an abode for ostriches.
public_domain_references.web: Thorns will come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it will be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.
public_domain_references.asv: And thorns shall come up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in the fortresses thereof; and it shall be a habitation of jackals, a court for ostriches.
public_domain_references.kjv: And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons, [and] a court for owls.
public_domain_references.brenton: And thorns shall spring up in their cities, and in her strong holds: and they shall be habitations of monsters, and a court for ostriches.

pob.text: And desert creatures will meet with hyenas[a], and the goat-demon will call to its fellow; indeed[b], there Lilith will settle down and find a resting place for herself.

spob.text: Desert creatures will meet hyenas,[a] and one goat-demon will call to another. Yes, Lilith[b] will settle there and find a place to rest.

public_domain_references.bsb: The desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and one wild goat will call to another. There the night creature will settle and find her place of repose.
public_domain_references.web: The wild animals of the desert will meet with the wolves, and the wild goat will cry to his fellow. Yes, the night creature shall settle there, and shall find herself a place of rest.
public_domain_references.asv: And the wild beasts of the desert shall meet with the wolves, and the wild goat shall cry to his fellow; yea, the night-monster shall settle there, and shall find her a place of rest.
public_domain_references.kjv: The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the wild beasts of the island, and the satyr shall cry to his fellow; the screech owl also shall rest there, and find for herself a place of rest.
public_domain_references.brenton: And devils shall meet with satyrs, and they shall cry one to the other: there shall satyrs rest, having found for themselves [a place of] rest.

pob.text: There the arrow snake will nest and lay eggs[a], and hatch them, and gather them in her shadow; indeed, there the kites will gather[c][b], each with her mate.

spob.text: There the arrow snake[a] will make its nest and lay its eggs. She will hatch them and shelter them in her shadow.[b] Yes, birds of prey called kites[c] will gather there, each with her mate.

public_domain_references.bsb: There the owl will make her nest; she will lay and hatch her eggs and gather her brood under her shadow. Even there the birds of prey will gather, each with its mate.
public_domain_references.web: The arrow snake will make her nest there, and lay, hatch, and gather under her shade. Yes, the kites will be gathered there, every one with her mate.
public_domain_references.asv: There shall the dart-snake make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shade; yea, there shall the kites be gathered, every one with her mate.
public_domain_references.kjv: There shall the great owl make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shadow: there shall the vultures also be gathered, every one with her mate.
public_domain_references.brenton: There has the hedgehog made its nest, and the earth has safely preserved its young: there have the deer met, and seen one another's faces.

pob.text: Search in the book of Yahweh and read: not one of these will be missing[a]; none will lack her mate. For his mouth has commanded[b], and his Spirit has gathered them.

spob.text: Search through Yahweh’s book and read it. Not one of these creatures will be missing. Each one will have her mate. For he has given the command with his mouth[a], and his Spirit[b] has gathered them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Search and read the scroll of the LORD: Not one of these will go missing, not one will lack her mate, because He has ordered it by His mouth, and He will gather them by His Spirit.
public_domain_references.web: Search in the book of Yahweh, and read: not one of these will be missing. None will lack her mate. For my mouth has commanded, and his Spirit has gathered them.
public_domain_references.asv: Seek ye out of the book of Jehovah, and read: no one of these shall be missing, none shall want her mate; for my mouth, it hath commanded, and his Spirit, it hath gathered them.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them.
public_domain_references.brenton: They passed by in [full] number, and not one of them perished: they sought not one another; for the Lord commanded them, and his Spirit gathered them.

pob.text: And he himself has cast the lot for them[a], and his hand has apportioned it to them by line; they will possess it forever[b]; from generation to generation they will dwell in it.

spob.text: He himself has used the lot to assign the land to them. With his hand, he has measured out the land with a measuring line and assigned it to them. They will possess[a] it forever, and generation after generation they will live there.

public_domain_references.bsb: He has allotted their portion; His hand has distributed it by measure. They will possess it forever; they will dwell in it from generation to generation.
public_domain_references.web: He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided it to them with a measuring line. They shall possess it forever. From generation to generation they will dwell in it.
public_domain_references.asv: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever; from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he shall cast lots for them, and his hand has portioned out [their] pasture, [saying], Ye shall inherit [the land] for ever: they shall rest on it [through] all generations.

pob.text: The wilderness and the dry land will rejoice[a]; the desert plain will be glad and blossom like the crocus.

spob.text: The wilderness and parched land will rejoice. The desert plain will be glad and bloom like a crocus.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: The wilderness and the land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
public_domain_references.web: The wilderness and the dry land will be glad. The desert will rejoice and blossom like a rose.
public_domain_references.asv: The wilderness and the dry land shall be glad; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.
public_domain_references.kjv: The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose.
public_domain_references.brenton: Be glad, thou thirsty desert: let the wilderness exult, and flower as the lily.

pob.text: It will blossom abundantly and rejoice—yes[a], with rejoicing and a shout of joy. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the majesty of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of Yahweh[c][b], the majesty of our God.

spob.text: It will be covered with blossoms. It will rejoice greatly and shout for joy. It will receive the glory of Lebanon and the majesty of Carmel and Sharon.[a] They[b] will see the glory of Yahweh, the majesty of our God.

public_domain_references.bsb: It will bloom profusely and rejoice with joy and singing. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
public_domain_references.web: It will blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Lebanon’s glory will be given to it, the excellence of Carmel and Sharon. They will see Yahweh’s glory, the excellence of our God.
public_domain_references.asv: It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing; the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon: they shall see the glory of Jehovah, the excellency of our God.
public_domain_references.kjv: It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon, they shall see the glory of the LORD, [and] the excellency of our God.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the desert places of Jordan shall blossom and rejoice; the glory of Libanus has been given to it, and the honour of Carmel; and my people shall see the glory of the Lord, and the majesty of God.

pob.text: Strengthen weak hands[a], and make firm feeble knees.

spob.text: Give strength to weak hands, and steady knees that are giving way.

public_domain_references.bsb: Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees!
public_domain_references.web: Strengthen the weak hands, and make the feeble knees firm.
public_domain_references.asv: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees.
public_domain_references.brenton: Be strong, ye relaxed hands and palsied knees.

pob.text: Say to those with an anxious heart[a], “Be strong; do not fear. Look, your God will come with vengeance, with the recompense of God[b]; he himself will come and save you.”

spob.text: Tell those whose hearts are anxious, “Be strong. Do not be afraid. Look! Your God will come with vengeance and God’s repayment.[a] He himself will come and save you.”

public_domain_references.bsb: Say to those with anxious hearts: “Be strong, do not fear! Behold, your God will come with vengeance. With divine retribution He will come to save you.”
public_domain_references.web: Tell those who have a fearful heart, “Be strong! Don’t be afraid! Behold, your God will come with vengeance, God’s retribution. He will come and save you.
public_domain_references.asv: Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come [with] vengeance, [with] the recompense of God; he will come and save you.
public_domain_references.kjv: Say to them [that are] of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come [with] vengeance, [even] God [with] a recompence; he will come and save you.
public_domain_references.brenton: Comfort one another, ye faint-hearted; be strong, fear not; behold, our God renders judgment, and he will render [it]; he will come and save us.

pob.text: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened[a], and the ears of the deaf will be opened.

spob.text: Then blind people’s eyes will be opened so they can see, and deaf people’s ears will be unstopped[a] so they can hear.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
public_domain_references.web: Then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will be unstopped.
public_domain_references.asv: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then shall the eyes of the blind be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall hear.

pob.text: Then the lame will leap like a deer[a], and the tongue of the mute will sing for joy; for waters have burst forth in the wilderness[b], and streams in the desert plain.

spob.text: Then a lame person will leap like a deer, and a mute person’s tongue will sing for joy.[a] For water has burst out in the wilderness, and streams have burst out in the desert plain.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the lame will leap like a deer and the mute tongue will shout for joy. For waters will gush forth in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
public_domain_references.web: Then the lame man will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will sing; for waters will break out in the wilderness, and streams in the desert.
public_domain_references.asv: Then shall the lame man leap as a hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall sing; for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then shall the lame [man] leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert.
public_domain_references.brenton: Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the stammerers shall speak plainly; for water has burst forth in the desert, and a channel [of water] in a thirsty land.

pob.text: The burning sand will become a pool[a], and the thirsty ground springs of water; in the haunt of jackals, where they lie down, there will be grass, reeds[c][b], and rushes.

spob.text: The burning sand[a] will become a pool, and the thirsty ground will become springs of water. Where jackals make their home and lie down,[b] grass, reeds, and rushes will grow.

public_domain_references.bsb: The parched ground will become a pool, the thirsty land springs of water. In the haunt where jackals once lay, there will be grass and reeds and papyrus.
public_domain_references.web: The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. Grass with reeds and rushes will be in the habitation of jackals, where they lay.
public_domain_references.asv: And the glowing sand shall become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water: in the habitation of jackals, where they lay, shall be grass with reeds and rushes.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water: in the habitation of dragons, where each lay, [shall be] grass with reeds and rushes.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the dry land shall become pools, and a fountain of water shall [be poured] into the thirsty land; there shall there be a joy of birds, ready habitations and marshes.

pob.text: And there shall be a highway there[a], and a road, and it shall be called the Holy Way. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it shall be for them[b]; whoever walks on the way—even fools—shall not go astray.

spob.text: A highway will be there, a road called the Holy Way. No one who is unclean[a] will travel on it. This way will be for God’s people.[b] Anyone who travels on it, even a fool, will not go astray.

public_domain_references.bsb: And there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it— only those who walk in the Way— and fools will not stray onto it.
public_domain_references.web: A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called “The Holy Way”. The unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked fools shall not go there.
public_domain_references.asv: And a highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for [the redeemed]: the wayfaring men, yea fools, shall not err [therein].
public_domain_references.kjv: And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it [shall be] for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err [therein].
public_domain_references.brenton: There shall be there a pure way, and it shall be called a holy way; and there shall not pass by there any unclean person, neither shall there be there an unclean way; but the dispersed shall walk on it, and they shall not go astray.

pob.text: No lion will be there[a], and no ravenous beast will go up on it; it will not be found there[c][b], but the redeemed will walk there.

spob.text: No lion will be there. No ravenous wild animal will come onto that road or be found there. But the redeemed will walk there.[a][b]

public_domain_references.bsb: No lion will be there, and no vicious beast will go up on it. Such will not be found there, but the redeemed will walk upon it.
public_domain_references.web: No lion will be there, nor will any ravenous animal go up on it. They will not be found there; but the redeemed will walk there.
public_domain_references.asv: No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast go up thereon; they shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk [there]:
public_domain_references.kjv: No lion shall be there, nor [any] ravenous beast shall go up thereon, it shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk [there:]
public_domain_references.brenton: And there shall be no lion there, neither shall any evil beast go up upon it, nor at all be found there; but the redeemed and gathered on the Lord's behalf, shall walk in it,

pob.text: And the redeemed of Yahweh will return and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy will be upon their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them[a], and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

spob.text: Those Yahweh has redeemed[a] will return. They will come to Zion singing. Joy that lasts forever will rest on their heads like a crown. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.

public_domain_references.bsb: So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee.
public_domain_references.web: Then Yahweh’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.”
public_domain_references.asv: and the ransomed of Jehovah shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads: they shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
public_domain_references.brenton: and shall return, and come to Sion with joy, and everlasting joy [shall be] over their head; for on their head [shall be] praise and exultation, and joy shall take possession of them: sorrow and pain, and groaning have fled away.

pob.text: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

spob.text: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah’s reign, King Sennacherib of Assyria attacked all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

public_domain_references.bsb: In the fourteenth year of Hezekiah’s reign, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked and captured all the fortified cities of Judah.
public_domain_references.web: Now in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked all of the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
public_domain_references.asv: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and took them.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, [that] Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of the reign of Ezekias, [that] Sennacherim, king of the Assyrians, came up against the strong cities of Judea, and took them.

pob.text: Then the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a heavy force. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool, on the highway to the launderer’s field.

spob.text: Then the king of Assyria sent his high official, the Rabshakeh,[a] from Lachish to Jerusalem, to King Hezekiah, with a powerful military force. The Rabshakeh took his position beside the water channel of the upper pool, on the road to the launderers’ field.

public_domain_references.bsb: And the king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh, with a great army, from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. And he stopped by the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road to the Launderer’s Field.
public_domain_references.web: The king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem to King Hezekiah with a large army. He stood by the aqueduct from the upper pool in the fuller’s field highway.
public_domain_references.asv: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the king of the Assyrians sent Rabsaces out of Laches to Jerusalem to king Ezekias with a large force: and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the way of the fuller's field.

pob.text: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah[a], who was over the household, came out to him, along with Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph[d][c][b], the recorder.

spob.text: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the official in charge of the royal household, came out to meet him. Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph, the royal recorder, came with him.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah the palace administrator, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder, went out to him.
public_domain_references.web: Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph the recorder came out to him.
public_domain_references.asv: Then came forth unto him Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, the son of Asaph, the recorder.
public_domain_references.kjv: Then came forth unto him Eliakim, Hilkiah’s son, which was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaph’s son, the recorder.
public_domain_references.brenton: And there went forth to him Heliakim the steward, the [son] of Chelcias, and Somnas the scribe, and Joach the [son] of Asaph, the recorder.

pob.text: Then the Rabshakeh said to them[a], “Please say to Hezekiah, ‘Thus says the great king[b], the king of Assyria: What is this confidence that you have trusted in?’”

spob.text: Then the Rabshakeh[a] said to them, “Please tell Hezekiah, ‘This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What are you trusting in that gives you this confidence?’”

public_domain_references.bsb: The Rabshakeh said to them, “Tell Hezekiah that this is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is the basis of this confidence of yours?
public_domain_references.web: Rabshakeh said to them, “Now tell Hezekiah, ‘The great king, the king of Assyria, says, “What confidence is this in which you trust?
public_domain_references.asv: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And Rabshakeh said unto them, Say ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence [is] this wherein thou trustest?
public_domain_references.brenton: And Rabsaces said to them, Say to Ezekias, Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians, Why art thou secure?

pob.text: You say—but they are only words of the lips—‘There is counsel and strength for war.’ Now in whom have you trusted, that you have rebelled against me?

public_domain_references.bsb: Behold, the Lord GOD comes with might, and His arm establishes His rule. His reward is with Him, and His recompense accompanies Him.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, the Lord Yahweh will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, the Lord Jehovah will come as a mighty one, and his arm will rule for him: Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense before him.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, the Lord GOD will come with strong [hand], and his arm shall rule for him: behold, his reward [is] with him, and his work before him.
public_domain_references.brenton: Behold the Lord! The Lord is coming with strength, and [his] arm is with power: behold, his reward is with him, and [his] work before him.

pob.text: Like a shepherd he will pasture his flock[a]; with his arm he will gather the lambs, and in his bosom he will carry them[c][b]; he will gently lead the nursing ewes.

spob.text: He will tend his flock like a shepherd. With his arm he will gather the lambs and carry them close to his chest. He will gently lead the mother sheep that are nursing their young.

public_domain_references.bsb: He tends His flock like a shepherd; He gathers the lambs in His arms and carries them close to His heart. He gently leads the nursing ewes.
public_domain_references.web: He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.
public_domain_references.asv: He will feed his flock like a shepherd, he will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom, [and] will gently lead those that have their young.
public_domain_references.kjv: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry [them] in his bosom, [and] shall gently lead those that are with young.
public_domain_references.brenton: He shall tend his flock as a shepherd, and he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and shall soothe them that are with young.

pob.text: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand[a], and marked off the heavens with a span, and measured the dust of the earth in a measure[c][b], and weighed the mountains in scales and the hills in balances?

spob.text: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand? Who has measured the heavens with the span of his hand and measured the dust of the earth in a measuring container?[a] Who has weighed the mountains on scales and the hills on a balance?

public_domain_references.bsb: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, or marked off the heavens with the span of his hand? Who has held the dust of the earth in a basket, or weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills with a balance?
public_domain_references.web: Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the dust of the earth in a measuring basket, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
public_domain_references.asv: Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and meted out heaven with the span, and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?
public_domain_references.brenton: Who has measured the water in his hand, and the heaven with a span, and all the earth in a handful? Who has weighed the mountains in scales, and the forests in a balance?

pob.text: Who has measured the Spirit of Yahweh[b][a], or what man has made his counsel known to him?

spob.text: Has anyone ever measured[b] Yahweh’s Spirit?[a] Has any man ever made his counsel known to him?

public_domain_references.bsb: Who has directed the Spirit of the LORD, or informed Him as His counselor?
public_domain_references.web: Who has directed Yahweh’s Spirit, or has taught him as his counselor?
public_domain_references.asv: Who hath directed the Spirit of Jehovah, or being his counsellor hath taught him?
public_domain_references.kjv: Who hath directed the Spirit of the LORD, or [being] his counsellor hath taught him?
public_domain_references.brenton: Who has known the mind of the Lord? and who has been his counsellor, to instruct him?

pob.text: Whom did he consult[a], and who gave him understanding? Who taught him the path of justice, taught him knowledge[b], and made known to him the way of understanding?

spob.text: Whom did he ask for advice? Who gave him understanding? Who taught him the path of justice,[a] taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Whom did He consult to enlighten Him, and who taught Him the paths of justice? Who imparted knowledge to Him and showed Him the way of understanding?
public_domain_references.web: Who did he take counsel with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
public_domain_references.asv: With whom took he counsel, and who instructed him, and taught him in the path of justice, and taught him knowledge, and showed to him the way of understanding?
public_domain_references.kjv: With whom took he counsel, and [who] instructed him, and taught him in the path of judgment, and taught him knowledge, and shewed to him the way of understanding?
public_domain_references.brenton: Or with whom has he taken counsel, and he has instructed him? or who has taught him judgment, or who has taught him the way of understanding;

pob.text: Look[a], the nations are like a drop from a bucket, and are regarded as dust on the scales; look[b], the coastlands he lifts like fine dust.

spob.text: Look! The nations are like a drop from a bucket. They count as dust on the scales. Look! The coastlands[a] are like fine dust when he lifts them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Surely the nations are like a drop in a bucket; they are considered a speck of dust on the scales; He lifts up the islands like fine dust.
public_domain_references.web: Behold, the nations are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of dust on a balance. Behold, he lifts up the islands like a very little thing.
public_domain_references.asv: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket, and are accounted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.
public_domain_references.kjv: Behold, the nations [are] as a drop of a bucket, and are counted as the small dust of the balance: behold, he taketh up the isles as a very little thing.
public_domain_references.brenton: since all the nations are counted as a drop from a bucket, and as the turning of a balance, [and] shall be counted as spittle?

pob.text: Lebanon is not enough to burn[b][a], nor are its animals enough for a burnt offering.

spob.text: Even all the wood of Lebanon would not be enough to fuel the fire, nor would all its animals be enough for a burnt offering.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel, nor its animals enough for a burnt offering.
public_domain_references.web: Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor its animals sufficient for a burnt offering.
public_domain_references.asv: And Lebanon is not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt-offering.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Lebanon [is] not sufficient to burn, nor the beasts thereof sufficient for a burnt offering.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Libanus is not enough to burn, nor all beasts enough for a whole-burnt offering:

pob.text: All the nations are as nothing before him[a]; they are regarded by him as less than nothing and emptiness.

spob.text: All the nations are like nothing compared with him. In his judgment, they are less than nothing; they are emptiness.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: All the nations are as nothing before Him; He regards them as nothingness and emptiness.
public_domain_references.web: All the nations are like nothing before him. They are regarded by him as less than nothing, and vanity.
public_domain_references.asv: All the nations are as nothing before him; they are accounted by him as less than nothing, and vanity.
public_domain_references.kjv: All nations before him [are] as nothing; and they are counted to him less than nothing, and vanity.
public_domain_references.brenton: and all the nations are as nothing, and counted as nothing.

pob.text: To whom[a], then, will you liken God, and what likeness will you compare to him?

spob.text: Who, then, will you compare God to? What likeness will you set beside him?

public_domain_references.bsb: To whom will you liken God? To what image will you compare Him?
public_domain_references.web: To whom then will you liken God? Or what likeness will you compare to him?
public_domain_references.asv: To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ To whom then will ye liken God? or what likeness will ye compare unto him?
public_domain_references.brenton: To whom have ye compared the Lord? and with what likeness have ye compared him?

pob.text: As for the idol, a craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold and forges silver chains for it.

spob.text: A craftsman casts an idol. Then a goldsmith covers it with gold and forges silver chains for it.

public_domain_references.bsb: To an idol that a craftsman casts and a metalworker overlays with gold and fits with silver chains?
public_domain_references.web: A workman has cast an image, and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts silver chains for it.
public_domain_references.asv: The image, a workman hath cast [it], and the goldsmith overlayeth it with gold, and casteth [for it] silver chains.
public_domain_references.kjv: The workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold, and casteth silver chains.
public_domain_references.brenton: Has not the artificer made an image, or the goldsmith having melted gold, gilt it over, [and] made it a similitude?

pob.text: He who is too poor for an offering chooses wood that will not rot[c][b][a]; he seeks out for himself a skilled craftsman to prepare an idol that will not totter.

spob.text: A person who is too poor to afford an offering[a] chooses wood that will not rot. He finds a skilled craftsman to make him an idol that will not wobble.

public_domain_references.bsb: To one bereft of an offering who chooses wood that will not rot, who seeks a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple?
public_domain_references.web: He who is too impoverished for such an offering chooses a tree that will not rot. He seeks a skillful workman to set up a carved image for him that will not be moved.
public_domain_references.asv: He that is too impoverished for [such] an oblation chooseth a tree that will not rot; he seeketh unto him a skilful workman to set up a graven image, that shall not be moved.
public_domain_references.kjv: He that [is] so impoverished that he hath no oblation chooseth a tree [that] will not rot; he seeketh unto him a cunning workman to prepare a graven image, [that] shall not be moved.
public_domain_references.brenton: For the artificer chooses out a wood that will not rot, and will wisely enquire how he shall set up his image, and [that so] that it should not be moved.

pob.text: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been told to you from the beginning? Have you not understood from the foundations of the earth?[a]

spob.text: Do you not know? Have you not heard? Have you not been told from the beginning? Have you not understood since the foundations of the earth were laid?[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been declared to you from the beginning? Have you not understood since the foundation of the earth?
public_domain_references.web: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? Haven’t you been told from the beginning? Haven’t you understood from the foundations of the earth?
public_domain_references.asv: Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?
public_domain_references.kjv: Have ye not known? have ye not heard? hath it not been told you from the beginning? have ye not understood from the foundations of the earth?
public_domain_references.brenton: Will ye not know? will ye not hear? has it not been told you of old? Have ye not known the foundations of the earth?

pob.text: He is the one who sits above the circle of the earth[a], and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers[b]; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.

spob.text: He sits above the circle of the earth,[a] and the people who live there are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a thin curtain[b] and spreads them out like a tent to live in.

public_domain_references.bsb: He sits enthroned above the circle of the earth; its dwellers are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.
public_domain_references.web: It is he who sits above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the heavens like a curtain, and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in,
public_domain_references.asv: [It is] he that sitteth above the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in;
public_domain_references.kjv: [It is] he that sitteth upon the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants thereof [are] as grasshoppers; that stretcheth out the heavens as a curtain, and spreadeth them out as a tent to dwell in:
public_domain_references.brenton: [It is] he that comprehends the circle of the earth, and the inhabitants in it are as grasshoppers; he that set up the heaven as a chamber, and stretched [it] out as a tent to dwell in:

pob.text: who brings princes to nothing[b][a], and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.

spob.text: He reduces princes to nothing. He makes the earth’s judges no more substantial than emptiness.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He brings the princes to nothing and makes the rulers of the earth meaningless.
public_domain_references.web: who brings princes to nothing, who makes the judges of the earth meaningless.
public_domain_references.asv: that bringeth princes to nothing; that maketh the judges of the earth as vanity.
public_domain_references.kjv: That bringeth the princes to nothing; he maketh the judges of the earth as vanity.
public_domain_references.brenton: he that appoints princes to rule as nothing, and has made the earth as nothing.

pob.text: Scarcely are they planted[a], scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the earth, when he merely blows on them and they wither[b], and a storm carries them away like stubble.

spob.text: They have only just been planted. They have only just been sown. Their stem has barely begun to take root in the ground. Then he only has to blow on them, and they wither. A storm carries them away like leftover stalks after harvest.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, no sooner have their stems taken root in the ground, than He blows on them and they wither, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble.
public_domain_references.web: They are planted scarcely. They are sown scarcely. Their stock has scarcely taken root in the ground. He merely blows on them, and they wither, and the whirlwind takes them away as stubble.
public_domain_references.asv: Yea, they have not been planted; yea, they have not been sown; yea, their stock hath not taken root in the earth: moreover he bloweth upon them, and they wither, and the whirlwind taketh them away as stubble.
public_domain_references.kjv: Yea, they shall not be planted; yea, they shall not be sown: yea, their stock shall not take root in the earth: and he shall also blow upon them, and they shall wither, and the whirlwind shall take them away as stubble.
public_domain_references.brenton: For they shall not plant, neither shall they sow, neither shall their root be fixed in the ground: he has blown upon them, and they are withered, and a storm shall carry them away like sticks.

pob.text: To whom then will you compare me[a], that I should be equal? says the Holy One.

spob.text: The Holy One says, “Who, then, will you compare me to?[a] Who is my equal?”

public_domain_references.bsb: “To whom will you liken Me, or who is My equal?” asks the Holy One.
public_domain_references.web: “To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?” says the Holy One.
public_domain_references.asv: To whom then will ye liken me, that I should be equal [to him]? saith the Holy One.
public_domain_references.kjv: To whom then will ye liken me, or shall I be equal? saith the Holy One.
public_domain_references.brenton: Now then to whom have ye compared me, that I may be exalted? saith the Holy One.

pob.text: Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host by number[a], calling all of them by name. Because of the greatness of his might and the strength of his power[c][b], not one is missing.

spob.text: Look up and see: Who created these? He is the one who brings out their whole array in order and calls them all by name. His might is so great and his power so strong that not one is missing.

public_domain_references.bsb: Lift up your eyes on high: Who created all these? He leads forth the starry host by number; He calls each one by name. Because of His great power and mighty strength, not one of them is missing.
public_domain_references.web: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who has created these, who brings out their army by number. He calls them all by name. By the greatness of his might, and because he is strong in power, not one is lacking.
public_domain_references.asv: Lift up your eyes on high, and see who hath created these, that bringeth out their host by number; he calleth them all by name; by the greatness of his might, and for that he is strong in power, not one is lacking.
public_domain_references.kjv: Lift up your eyes on high, and behold who hath created these [things], that bringeth out their host by number: he calleth them all by names by the greatness of his might, for that [he is] strong in power; not one faileth.
public_domain_references.brenton: Lift up your eyes on high, and see, who has displayed all these things? [even] he that brings forth his host by number: he shall call them all by name by [means of his] great glory, and by the power of his might: nothing has escaped thee.

pob.text: Why do you say[a], O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, “My way is hidden from Yahweh, and my justice is disregarded by my God”?

spob.text: Jacob, why do you say this? Israel, why do you speak this way: “The path of my life is hidden from Yahweh, and my God ignores my claim for justice”?[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Why do you say, O Jacob, and why do you assert, O Israel, “My way is hidden from the LORD, and my claim is ignored by my God”?
public_domain_references.web: Why do you say, Jacob, and speak, Israel, “My way is hidden from Yahweh, and the justice due me is disregarded by my God”?
public_domain_references.asv: Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, My way is hid from Jehovah, and the justice [due] to me is passed away from my God?
public_domain_references.kjv: Why sayest thou, O Jacob, and speakest, O Israel, My way is hid from the LORD, and my judgment is passed over from my God?
public_domain_references.brenton: For say not thou, O Jacob, and why hast thou spoken, Israel, [saying], My way is hid from God, and my God has taken away [my] judgment, and has departed?

pob.text: Have you not known? Have you not heard? Yahweh is the everlasting God[a], the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow faint or become weary; his understanding is unsearchable.

spob.text: Don’t you know? Haven’t you heard? Yahweh is the everlasting God, the Creator of the farthest reaches of the earth. He never grows faint or weary. No one can fully search out his understanding.

public_domain_references.bsb: Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary; His understanding is beyond searching out.
public_domain_references.web: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.
public_domain_references.asv: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard? The everlasting God, Jehovah, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary; there is no searching of his understanding.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, [that] the everlasting God, the LORD, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? [there is] no searching of his understanding.
public_domain_references.brenton: And now, hast thou not known? hast thou not heard? the eternal God, the God that formed the ends of the earth, shall not hunger, nor be weary, and there is no searching of his understanding.

pob.text: He gives strength to the weary[a], and to the one without vigor he increases might.

spob.text: He gives strength to the weary and increases the power of those who have no strength.

public_domain_references.bsb: He gives power to the faint and increases the strength of the weak.
public_domain_references.web: He gives power to the weak. He increases the strength of him who has no might.
public_domain_references.asv: He giveth power to the faint; and to him that hath no might he increaseth strength.
public_domain_references.kjv: He giveth power to the faint; and to [them that have] no might he increaseth strength.
public_domain_references.brenton: He gives strength to the hungry, and sorrow to them that are not suffering.

pob.text: Even young men grow faint and become weary[a], and young men surely stumble.

spob.text: Even young men grow faint and tired; young men in their prime will surely stumble.

public_domain_references.bsb: Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall.
public_domain_references.web: Even the youths faint and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;
public_domain_references.asv: Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall:
public_domain_references.kjv: Even the youths shall faint and be weary, and the young men shall utterly fall:
public_domain_references.brenton: For the young [men] shall hunger, and the youths shall be weary, and the choice [men] shall be powerless:

pob.text: But those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength[a]; they will rise up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary[b]; they will walk and not faint.

spob.text: But those who wait for Yahweh[a] will gain new strength. They will rise on wings like eagles.[b] They will run without growing weary; they will walk without fainting.

public_domain_references.bsb: But those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength; they will mount up with wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not faint.
public_domain_references.web: but those who wait for Yahweh will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
public_domain_references.asv: but they that wait for Jehovah shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not faint.
public_domain_references.kjv: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew [their] strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; [and] they shall walk, and not faint.
public_domain_references.brenton: but they that wait on God shall renew [their] strength; they shall put forth new feathers like eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; they shall walk, and not hunger.

pob.text: Be silent before me[a], coastlands; let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near; then let them speak[c][b]. Together let us draw near for judgment.

spob.text: Distant coastlands,[a] be silent before me. Let the peoples gather fresh strength. Then let them come near and speak. Together, let us come forward for judgment.

public_domain_references.bsb: “Be silent before Me, O islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come forward and testify; let us together draw near for judgment.
public_domain_references.web: “Keep silent before me, islands, and let the peoples renew their strength. Let them come near, then let them speak. Let’s meet together for judgment.
public_domain_references.asv: Keep silence before me, O islands; and let the peoples renew their strength: let them come near; then let them speak; let us come near together to judgment.
public_domain_references.kjv: Keep silence before me, O islands; and let the people renew [their] strength: let them come near; then let them speak: let us come near together to judgment.
public_domain_references.brenton: Hold a feast to me, ye islands: for the princes shall renew [their] strength: let them draw nigh and speak together: then let them declare judgment.

pob.text: Who has stirred up one from the east[a], calling him in righteousness to his feet? He gives nations before him and subdues kings; he gives them like dust to his sword[b], like driven stubble to his bow.

spob.text: Who has raised up a man from the east and summoned him in righteousness[a] to serve at his feet?[b] He hands nations over to this man and brings kings under his power.[c] He makes them like dust before the man’s sword and like wind-driven stubble before his bow.

public_domain_references.bsb: Who has aroused one from the east and called him to his feet in righteousness ? He hands nations over to him and subdues kings before him. He turns them to dust with his sword, to windblown chaff with his bow.
public_domain_references.web: Who has raised up one from the east? Who called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands over nations to him and makes him rule over kings. He gives them like the dust to his sword, like the driven stubble to his bow.
public_domain_references.asv: Who hath raised up one from the east, whom he calleth in righteousness to his foot? he giveth nations before him, and maketh him rule over kings; he giveth them as the dust to his sword, as the driven stubble to his bow.
public_domain_references.kjv: Who raised up the righteous [man] from the east, called him to his foot, gave the nations before him, and made [him] rule over kings? he gave [them] as the dust to his sword, [and] as driven stubble to his bow.
public_domain_references.brenton: Who raised up righteousness from the east, [and] called it to his feet, so that it should go? shall appoint [it] an adversary of Gentiles, and shall dismay kings, and bury their swords in the earth, and cast forth their bows and arrows as sticks?

pob.text: He pursues them and passes on safely[a], by a path his feet had not traveled.

spob.text: He pursues them and continues safely along a path his feet have never traveled before.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: He pursues them, going on safely, hardly touching the path with his feet.
public_domain_references.web: He pursues them and passes by safely, even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.
public_domain_references.asv: He pursueth them, and passeth on safely, even by a way that he had not gone with his feet.
public_domain_references.kjv: He pursued them, [and] passed safely; [even] by the way [that] he had not gone with his feet.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he shall pursue them; the way of his feet shall proceed in peace.

pob.text: Who has acted and done this[a], calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, am the first, and with the last ones—I am he.

spob.text: Who has acted and made all this happen, calling one generation after another from the beginning? I, Yahweh, am the first. I am also with the last generations[a]—I am he.

public_domain_references.bsb: Who has performed this and carried it out, calling forth the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD—the first and the last— I am He.”
public_domain_references.web: Who has worked and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Yahweh, the first, and with the last, I am he.”
public_domain_references.asv: Who hath wrought and done it, calling the generations from the beginning? I, Jehovah, the first, and with the last, I am he.
public_domain_references.kjv: Who hath wrought and done [it], calling the generations from the beginning? I the LORD, the first, and with the last; I [am] he.
public_domain_references.brenton: Who has wrought and done these things? he has called it who called it from the generations of old; I God, the first and to [all] futurity, I AM.

pob.text: The coastlands have seen and fear[a]; the ends of the earth tremble[b]. They draw near and come.

spob.text: The people of the coastal lands[a] have seen what God has done, and they are afraid. People at the ends of the earth tremble. They come near; they come.
